title.en: US to allow Iran delegation to attend UN meetings in New York as war passes half-year mark
title.zh: 美国允许伊朗代表团出席联合国会议，战争已过半年

summary.en: The US government has granted visas to Iranian officials, including President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, to attend UN meetings in New York. This decision comes as the war between the two countries enters its seventh month, with the Iranian delegation facing travel restrictions.
summary.zh: 美国政府已向包括总统马苏德·佩泽什基扬和外交部长阿巴斯·阿拉格奇在内的伊朗官员发放了签证，允许他们出席在纽约举行的联合国会议。此举发生在两国战争进入第七个月之际，伊朗代表团将受到旅行限制。

body.en:
The US government has granted visas to Iranian officials so they can travel to the UN General Assembly in New York next week, as the war between the two countries grinds into its seventh month.

The BBC understands the core delegation permitted to attend includes Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.

A spokesman for the US State Department confirmed the decision on Thursday, saying that the delegation will be placed under travel restrictions and will be banned from purchasing certain American products.

The move comes as the war shows no sign of ending. Since it began in February, it has driven up global energy prices, and expanded into neighbouring countries.

"Consistent with our host country obligations, the core delegation from the Iranian regime will be able to attend UN General Assembly High Level Week," a spokesman for the US State Department told the BBC.

"The delegation will be under travel restrictions and will face prohibitions on the purchase of luxury and other goods per our policy. The delegation is smaller than last year."

Last year, diplomats attending from Iran were banned from shopping at wholesale stores like Costco. They also were required to seek permission from the US before purchasing luxury goods, including jewellery, alcohol and cars.

State Department Spokesman Tommy Pigott said the US would prevent the diplomats from "going on shopping sprees" as the Iranian people deal with water and electricity shortages, "brutal repression", and "soaring inflation".

"We will not let the Iranian regime's elites exploit UNGA for a luxury retail splurge paid for by the Iranian people's suffering, all while the regime funnels Iran's wealth to support its terrorist proxies," he posted on X, warning New York shops to "be on guard" against selling goods to the delegation.

He did not indicate if the US was aware of any specific plans from the delegation to buy luxury items.

The 81st session of the UN General Assembly (UNGA) is currently underway. The General Debate - the centrepiece of the annual event - is due to begin on Tuesday.

Tuesday will include speeches from US President Donald Trump, UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, and France President Emmanuel Macron.

Wednesday is expected to see speeches from the leaders of Ukraine, Syria and Iran.

Public and political pressure has mounted on the White House to find an end to the conflict with Iran, which began on 28 February when the US and Israel launched joint attacks on the country.

Since the war began, Iran has repeatedly attacked US bases and allied states in the Gulf, as well as Israel.

The BBC recently learned that the US denied a visa to Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas and the Palestinian delegation to attend UNGA.

The White House, which...
body.zh: 美国政府已向伊朗官员发放签证，以便他们下周前往纽约参加联合国大会，此时两国之间的战争已进入第七个月。 据英国广播公司了解，获准出席的核心代表团包括伊朗总统马苏德·佩泽什基安和外交部长阿巴斯·阿拉格奇。 美国国务院发言人周四证实了这一决定，称该代表团将受到旅行限制，并被禁止购买某些美国产品。 此举是在战争没有结束迹象的情况下进行的。自2月份开始以来，它已经推高了全球能源价格，并扩展到了周边国家。 美国国务院发言人告诉英国广播公司：“根据我们东道国的义务，伊朗政权的核心代表团将能够参加联合国大会高级别周。” “根据我们的政策，代表团将受到旅行限制，并将面临购买奢侈品和其他商品的禁令。代表团规模比去年小。” 去年，来自伊朗的外交官被禁止在 Costco 等批发商店购物。他们还被要求在购买珠宝、酒类和汽车等奢侈品之前获得美国的许可。 美国国务院发言人汤米·皮戈特表示，在伊朗人民面临水电短缺、“残酷镇压”和“通货膨胀飙升”之际，美国将阻止外交官“疯狂购物”。 他在 X 上发帖称，“我们不会让伊朗政权的精英利用联大进行奢侈品零售挥霍，而伊朗人民的苦难却为他们买单，同时该政权却将伊朗的财富用于支持其恐怖主义代理人。”他警告纽约商店“警惕”，不要向代表团出售商品。 他没有表明美国是否知道代表团购买奢侈品的任何具体计划。 目前，第81届联合国大会（UNGA）正在召开。一般性辩论是年度活动的核心，将于周二开始。 周二，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普、英国首相安迪·伯纳姆和法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙将发表讲话。 预计周三乌克兰、叙利亚和伊朗领导人将发表讲话。 公众和政治压力不断加大，要求白宫结束与伊朗的冲突。这场冲突始于 2 月 28 日，当时美国和以色列对伊朗发动联合袭击。 自战争开始以来，伊朗多次袭击美国基地和海湾盟国以及以色列。 英国广播公司(BBC)近日获悉，美国拒绝向巴勒斯坦总统阿巴斯和出席联大的巴勒斯坦代表团发放签证。 白宫，其中...

reflection.en: As the conflict grinds into its seventh month, the US decision to grant visas for Iranian officials to attend UN meetings offers a fragile opening for dialogue. Even amidst deep hostility, the pursuit of peace, however difficult, remains a vital path.
reflection.zh: 随着冲突进入第七个月，美国允许伊朗官员出席联合国会议的决定为对话提供了一个脆弱的开端。即使在充满敌意的情况下，寻求和平的道路仍然至关重要，尽管它充满挑战。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: The EU wants a new kind of member — and Australia could be in the mix
title.zh: 欧盟想要一种新型成员——澳大利亚可能在其中

summary.en: European Parliament President Roberta Metsola has suggested that Australia and New Zealand could explore becoming "associate members" of the European Union, similar to arrangements with Canada, as the EU seeks to deepen relationships with key partners through various association models.
summary.zh: 欧洲议会主席罗伯塔·梅索拉建议，澳大利亚和新西兰可以探索成为欧盟的“联系成员”，类似于与加拿大的安排，因为欧盟寻求通过各种联合模式深化与关键伙伴的关系。

body.en:
Australia and New Zealand could follow in Canada's footsteps to become "associate members" of the European Union, a top EU official has suggested.

European Parliament President Roberta Metsola, in an interview with Europe Today, specifically brought up Australia and New Zealand as examples of countries that could deepen their relationships with the alliance.

Metsola said the EU had different models for its relationships with other countries, from full membership to participation in the European Economic Area, and was also looking to deepen ties with partners such as Canada — a model she expected other countries to pursue.

"I don't doubt that that will also include other countries that will come," she said.

"We've already seen it, both in terms of legislation that we pass, where we see partners from across the world — Australia, New Zealand being some examples — of saying, look, we want to deepen our relationship."

"We're doing it in terms of trade. We're doing it in terms of conversation on what we do with social media, with children, with critical raw materials, alliances that can be forged."

Canadian Prime ‌Minister Mark Carney has welcomed the proposal of becoming an "associate member" of the EU, saying Europe and Canada are stronger together ‌and should deepen ties to protect their citizens' prosperity.

"Europe and Canada are each strong. Europe and Canada are even stronger together," Carney told the European parliament in Strasbourg, France, on Thursday.

"I am not proposing a third bloc in order to become a great-power rival — only with better manners."

"We do not seek power to dominate others. On the contrary, we are pursuing ‌resilience so that ‌no one can ⁠control our open markets, impair our sovereignty, threaten our territorial integrity, or undermine our freedoms, our democracies, our rule of law."

Hours earlier, US President Donald Trump threatened to take action against the EU if it moved forward with European Commission President Ursula von der ‌Leyen's proposal of associate membership for Canada.

Both the EU and Canada have been facing stiff rivalry and pressure from the Trump administration on trade , among other matters, and from an increasingly assertive China.

"If they do that, if I think it's at all a hostile act, ⁠I will put very serious tariffs or stop trading with Europe on many ‌things," Trump told reporters en route to an event in North Carolina.

"If it's a good intention, that's fine. If it's a bad intention, we'll ‌put very heavy tariffs on Europe," he added.

body.zh: 一位欧盟高级官员表示，澳大利亚和新西兰可以追随加拿大的脚步，成为欧盟的“准成员”。 欧洲议会主席罗伯塔·梅索拉在接受《今日欧洲》采访时特别提到澳大利亚和新西兰作为可以加深与该联盟关系的国家的例子。 梅索拉表示，欧盟与其他国家的关系有不同的模式，从正式成员身份到参与欧洲经济区，并且还寻求加深与加拿大等合作伙伴的关系——她希望其他国家也能效仿这种模式。 “我毫不怀疑，其他国家也会来，”她说。 “我们已经看到了这一点，无论是在我们通过的立法方面，我们都看到来自世界各地的合作伙伴——澳大利亚、新西兰就是一些例子——说，看，我们希望加深我们的关系。” 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 “我们是在贸易方面这样做的。我们是在对话方面进行的，涉及我们如何处理社交媒体、儿童、关键原材料以及可以建立的联盟。” 加拿大总理马克·卡尼对成为欧盟“准成员”的提议表示欢迎，他表示欧洲和加拿大在一起更加强大，应该深化联系以保护其公民的繁荣。 卡尼周四在法国斯特拉斯堡的欧洲议会上表示：“欧洲和加拿大都很强大。欧洲和加拿大在一起甚至更强大。” “我提出建立第三集团并不是为了成为大国竞争对手——只是以更好的方式。” “我们并不寻求支配他人的权力。相反，我们正在追求韧性，以便任何人都无法控制我们的开放市场，损害我们的主权，威胁我们的领土完整，或破坏我们的自由、民主和法治。” 几个小时前，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普威胁称，如果欧盟继续推进欧盟委员会主席乌尔苏拉·冯德莱恩提出的加拿大准成员资格提案，将对欧盟采取行动。 欧盟和加拿大都面临着特朗普政府在贸易等问题上以及日益自信的中国的激烈竞争和压力。 特朗普在前往北卡罗来纳州举行的一次活动的途中对记者表示：“如果他们这样做，如果我认为这完全是一种敌对行为，我将征收非常严厉的关税或停止与欧洲在许多事情上的贸易。” “如果是善意，那也没关系。如果是恶意，我们将对欧洲征收非常高的关税，”他补充道。 欧盟委员会...

reflection.en: The European Union is exploring new ways to deepen its relationships with countries like Australia and New Zealand, moving beyond traditional membership models. This initiative highlights a diplomatic effort to build bridges and foster cooperation in an increasingly interconnected world. It calls to mind the biblical encouragement to pursue peace and live...
reflection.zh: 欧洲联盟正在探索与澳大利亚和新西兰等国深化关系的新途径，超越传统的成员国模式。这一举措凸显了建立桥梁和促进合作以应对日益互联世界的外交努力。这让人想起圣经中鼓励追求和平、与众人和睦相处的教导，并寻求建立建设性关系的方法。

title.en: Addison Lee founder owes £20.5m in tax after UK tribunal ruling
title.zh: Addison Lee创始人因英国法庭裁决欠税2050万英镑

summary.en: The founder of Addison Lee, John Griffin, owes £20.5 million in taxes after a tribunal rejected his claim to be a non-domicile, despite having lived in England since childhood and expressing a strong connection to Ireland. The ruling confirms HMRC's challenge to his tax status.
summary.zh: Addison Lee公司的创始人约翰·格里芬（John Griffin）因其被法庭驳回的非定居者身份主张而欠税2050万英镑，尽管他自童年起就居住在英格兰，并表达了与爱尔兰的深厚联系。该裁决证实了英国税务海关总署（HMRC）对其税务身份的质疑。

body.en: HMRC wins challenge over John Griffin’s claim to be non-dom despite having lived in England since childhood The founder of Addison Lee owes £20.5m in tax after a tribunal dismissed a claim that he should be treated as a nom-dom despite living in the UK since childhood. John Griffin had argued he should be treated as a nom-dom due to his connection to Ireland, saying: “I was and am besotted with Ireland, infatuated with Ireland. I believe that I have always been and am Irish.” Continue reading...
body.zh: 英国税务海关总署 (HMRC) 赢得了对约翰·格里芬 (John Griffin) 声称自己是非籍籍人士的质疑，尽管他从小就生活在英国。Addison Lee 的创始人声称，尽管他从小就生活在英国，但仍应被视为籍籍无名，但法庭驳回了他的主张，因此他欠了 2050 万英镑的税款。约翰·格里芬认为，由于他与爱尔兰的联系，他应该被视为匿名者，他说：“我过去和现在都迷恋爱尔兰，迷恋爱尔兰。我相信我一直都是爱尔兰人。”继续阅读...

Micah 6:8 reminds us that true righteousness involves acting justly, loving mercy, and walking humbly with our God. This principle calls for integrity in all dealings, whether personal or financial, ensuring that our actions...
reflection.zh: 财富的追求和税法的复杂性有时会模糊公平和问责的基本问题。弥迦书6:8提醒我们，真正的公义在于秉持公正、喜爱慈爱、谦卑地与神同行。这一原则要求我们在所有交往中都保持诚信，无论是个人还是财务方面，确保我们的行为符合道德标准并尊重管治社会的体系。

verse.textEn: What does Yahweh require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verse.textZh: 雅伟向你所要的是什么呢？只要你行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的神同行。

title.en: New cat species identified for first time in more than a century in Bolivia
title.zh: 玻利维亚发现百年新猫种

summary.en: A new species of wild feline, smaller than a domestic cat and known locally as 'tilcayo', has been identified in Bolivia's Yungas cloud forest. This marks the first formal naming and description of a new living cat species in over a century. The cat belongs to the tiger cat group and was found in the humid,...
summary.zh: 在玻利维亚的云雾林中发现了一种新的野生猫科动物物种，当地人称之为“tilcayo”，体型比家猫还小。这是100多年来首次正式命名和描述一种新的现存猫科动物物种。这种猫属于虎猫家族，生活在湿润、多山的永加斯地区。

body.en: New species of wild feline was discovered in Bolivia’s Yungas forest that is smaller than the average domestic ⁠cat A diminutive wild cat that inhabits Bolivia’s ⁠cloud forest has been identified as a previously unknown species, marking the first time a new living cat species has been formally named and described in more than a century. The cat, called tilcayo by local communities, is part of a group called tiger ⁠cats found across much of South ⁠America. It was found in Bolivia’s ​lush Yungas forest, a mountainous region where forests are often covered by clouds and surrounded by high humidity, according to researchers. It measures about 18in (46cm) long and weighs about 3lbs (1.4kg), making it smaller than the average domestic ⁠cat. Continue reading...
body.zh: 玻利维亚永加斯森林中发现了一种新的野生猫科动物，其体型比普通家猫还要小。栖息在玻利维亚云雾森林中的一种小型野猫已被确定为以前未知的物种，这标志着一个多世纪以来首次对一种新的现存猫科动物物种进行正式命名和描述。这只猫被当地社区称为蒂尔卡约（tilcayo），是南美洲大部分地区发现的虎猫族群的一部分。研究人员称，它是在玻利维亚茂密的永加斯森林中发现的，该地区的森林经常被云层覆盖，周围湿度很高。它长约 18 英寸（46 厘米），重约 3 磅（1.4 公斤），比普通家猫要小。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The discovery of the tilcayo in Bolivia's lush Yungas forest is a testament to the astonishing diversity of life Yahweh has created. Even in well-explored regions, new wonders await discovery, reminding us of the profound wisdom woven into the fabric of creation. This small feline, previously unknown to science, embodies the intricate beauty and mystery of...
reflection.zh: 在玻利维亚葱郁的永加斯森林中发现tilcayo，证明了雅伟所造生命的惊人多样性。即使在已充分探索的地区，新的奇迹仍在等待被发现，提醒我们创造的本质中蕴含着深刻的智慧。 这种此前科学界未知的小型猫科动物，体现了自然界错综复杂的美丽与神秘。它呼唤我们去欣赏生态系统的微妙平衡，以及雅伟通过祂所造之物不断展现的艺术。

verse.textEn: How many are your works, Yahweh! In wisdom you made them all; the earth is full of your creatures.
verse.textZh: 雅伟啊，你所造的何其多！都是你用智慧造成的；遍地满了你的丰富。

title.en: UN experts say grounds to believe US committed war crimes in Iran strikes
title.zh: 联合国专家称有理由相信美国在伊朗的袭击中犯下战争罪

summary.en: UN human rights experts stated there are reasonable grounds to believe that the US committed war crimes in two missile strikes in Iran during February. These strikes targeted a primary school in Minab and a sports complex in Lamerd, resulting in the deaths of at least 177 civilians and damage to civilian...
summary.zh: 联合国人权专家表示，有充分理由相信美国在今年二月于伊朗发动的两次导弹袭击中犯下了战争罪。这两次袭击分别针对米纳布的一所小学和拉梅尔德的一个体育场，造成至少177名平民死亡，并破坏了民用基础设施。美国尚未承认发动这些袭击，并曾否认袭击拉梅尔德，表示正在调查米纳布事件。报告还指出，伊朗当局在镇压反政府抗议活动期间犯下了危害...

body.en:
UN human rights experts say there are reasonable grounds to believe the US committed war crimes in two strikes in Iran that killed at least 177 civilians.

A new report by the Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Iran , external said February's missile strikes on a primary school in Minab and a sports complex in Lamerd constituted indiscriminate attacks causing civilian deaths and damage to civilian infrastructure.

The US previously denied striking Lamerd and said it was investigating what happened in Minab. A State Department official said the US did not give credibility to the findings in the report.

The experts also found Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity during a crackdown on mass anti-government protests in January.

They said killings by security forces occurred on "a staggering and unprecedented scale" across all 31 provinces.

Iran has also not yet commented on the findings, but it has previously rejected allegations of systematic violations of human rights.

'What was their crime?': BBC visits Iran school where strike killed 120 children

"Civilians in Iran are caught between gross human rights violations and crimes against humanity committed by their own government and the nation's deadly conflict with the United States and Israel," the fact-finding mission warned in a statement on Thursday.

For their latest report to the UN Human Rights Council, the mission's three independent experts investigated two of the deadliest attacks on civilians during the conflict.

On 28 February, when the US and Israel launched their war against Iran, Tomahawk missiles struck Shajareh Tayyebeh Primary School in the southern town of Minab, killing at least 156 people, including 120 children, according to local authorities.

The fact-finding mission's experts said the school was adjacent to an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) naval complex also attacked that day, but that the school was clearly identifiable and that no information indicated that it was used for military purposes.

The experts said that, based on the evidence gathered - including media reports indicating that a preliminary US military inquiry found US forces responsible, and the fact that the US is the only party to the conflict that possesses Tomahawk missiles - they had reasonable grounds to believe that the strike on the school was carried out by the US.

They also concluded that the school was "the intended point of impact and that the damage did not result from an errant strike or collateral damage" from the attack on the IRGC complex, citing survivors as saying the school was struck twice.

The US military has yet to release the findings of its investigation into the Minab strike, but Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has said it would "never target...
body.zh: 联合国人权专家表示，有合理的理由相信美国在对伊朗的两次袭击中犯下了战争罪，造成至少 177 名平民死亡。 伊朗问题独立国际实况调查团的一份新报告称，2月份对米纳布一所小学和拉默德一所体育场馆的导弹袭击构成不分青红皂白的袭击，造成平民死亡和民用基础设施损坏。 美国没有立即发表评论。它此前否认袭击了拉默德，并表示正在调查米纳布发生的事情。 专家们还发现伊朗当局在一月份镇压大规模反政府抗议活动时犯下了反人类罪。 他们表示，安全部队在所有 31 个省份发生的杀戮规模“令人震惊且前所未有”。 伊朗也尚未对调查结果发表评论，但此前已否认了系统性侵犯人权的指控。 “他们犯了什么罪？”：BBC 探访伊朗学校，罢工导致 120 名儿童死亡 实况调查团在周四的一份声明中警告说：“伊朗平民陷入了本国政府犯下的严重侵犯人权和反人类罪以及该国与美国和以色列的致命冲突之间。” 在向联合国人权理事会提交的最新报告中，特派团的三名独立专家调查了冲突期间针对平民的两起最致命的袭击事件。 据地方当局称，2 月 28 日，当美国和以色列对伊朗发动战争时，战斧导弹袭击了南部城镇米纳布的 Shajareh Tayyebeh 小学，造成至少 156 人死亡，其中包括 120 名儿童。 实况调查团的专家表示，该学校毗邻伊斯兰革命卫队（IRGC）海军基地，当天也遭到袭击，但该学校的身份清晰可辨，并且没有信息表明它被用于军事目的。 专家们表示，根据收集到的证据，包括媒体报道称美国军方初步调查发现美军应对此事负责，以及美国是冲突中唯一拥有战斧导弹的一方，他们有合理的理由相信对学校的袭击是美国所为。 他们还得出结论，学校是伊斯兰革命卫队综合体袭击中“预定的撞击点，造成的损害不是错误的袭击或附带损害造成的”，并援引幸存者的话说，学校遭到了两次袭击。 美国军方尚未公布对米纳布袭击事件的调查结果，但国防部长皮特·赫格斯表示，美国军方“永远不会针对平民目标”。 同样在 2 月 28 日，Precision...

reflection.en: The report from UN experts raises grave concerns about civilian casualties in conflict. The cycle of violence, where actions by one party may lead to devastating responses, traps communities in suffering. Scripture calls us to actively resist this pattern, urging, 'Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.' (Romans 12:21)
reflection.zh: 联合国专家的报告提出了对冲突中平民伤亡的严重关切。暴力循环，即一方的行为可能导致毁灭性的回应，使社区陷入痛苦。经文呼吁我们积极抵制这种模式，劝勉说：“不要被恶所胜，反要以善胜恶。”（罗马书 12:21）

verse.textEn: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
verse.textZh: 你不可为恶所胜，反要以善胜恶。

title.en: Suspect in ‘Putney pusher’ case told family that investigation was ‘murdering him’
title.zh: “普特尼推搡者”案嫌疑人告诉家人调查“正在杀死他”

summary.en: Nicholas Brandram, 44, suspected in the "Putney pusher" case, died by suicide. His sisters revealed that in the days before his death, he expressed that the police investigation and online abuse were destroying his mental health, stating he had "no fight left."
summary.zh: 44岁的尼古拉斯·布兰德拉姆（Nicholas Brandram）是“普特尼推搡者”案的嫌疑人，他已自杀身亡。他的姐妹们透露，在他去世前几天，他表示警方调查和网络辱骂正在摧毁他的精神健康，并说他“再也无力反抗”。

body.en: Exclusive: Sisters of Nicholas Brandram recount 44-year-old’s deteriorating mental health in days before he took his life Days before Nicholas Brandram, the man suspected of being the “Putney pusher”, killed himself, he told his family that the police investigation was “murdering him”. He had “no fight left” in him, he told his sisters, Alexia Hicks and Sophie Voelcker, and could not see an end to the Metropolitan police investigation, or the online abuse. Continue reading...
body.zh: 独家：尼古拉斯·布兰德拉姆 (Nicholas Brandram) 的姐妹们讲述了 44 岁的尼古拉斯·布兰德拉姆 (Nicholas Brandram) 自杀前几天精神健康状况不断恶化的情况。 涉嫌“普特尼推手”的男子尼古拉斯·布兰德拉姆 (Nicholas Brandram) 自杀前几天，他告诉家人，警方的调查正在“谋杀他”。他告诉他的姐妹亚历克西娅·希克斯（Alexia Hicks）和索菲·沃尔克（Sophie Voelcker），他“已经没有战斗力了”，而且看不到伦敦警察厅的调查或网上虐待的结束。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The intense pressure of a police investigation and relentless online abuse can feel like an unbearable weight, crushing a person's spirit. In such moments of deep despair, the ancient promise is that Yahweh is near to the brokenhearted, offering a presence even when all human comfort seems lost.
reflection.zh: 警方调查的巨大压力和无情的网络辱骂，会成为一种无法承受的重负，压垮人的精神。在如此深切的绝望时刻，古老的应许是雅伟靠近心碎的人，即使在所有人类的安慰似乎都已消失时，祂仍同在。

verse.textEn: Yahweh is close to the brokenhearted and saves those who are crushed in spirit.
verse.textZh: 雅伟靠近伤心的人，拯救灵性痛悔的人。

title.en: Why Canadians are ready for closer ties with Europe
title.zh: 为什么加拿大人渴望与欧洲建立更紧密的关系

summary.en: Canadians are expressing enthusiasm for closer ties with the European Union, particularly the prospect of living, working, and studying within the EU. This sentiment was sparked by Prime Minister Mark Carney's recent speech proposing Canada become an "associate member" and urging deeper cooperation.
summary.zh: 加拿大人对与欧洲联盟建立更紧密关系的前景表示兴奋，特别是生活、工作和学习的机会。这一情绪源于总理马克·卡尼（Mark Carney）最近在演讲中提出的建议，希望加拿大成为其“准成员国”，并呼吁深化合作。

body.en:
Miriam Levin-Gold likes Prime Minister Mark Carney's idea of Canadians being able to live and work in the European Union under proposed closer ties with the trade bloc.

"I think that's great for young people to explore different parts of the world and work in different places and have different experiences," the commuter told the BBC in Toronto.

Canadians woke up to news of Carney's speech to the European Parliament in Strasbourg on Thursday morning, welcoming the EU's ambition for Canada to become its first "associate member" as he urged closer co-operation on defence and energy.

"We should deepen our people-to-people ties, allowing our youth to live, work and study where they want on either side of the Atlantic," the PM said.

Carney told MEPs that Canada and Europe were "stronger together" in the face of "geopolitical rupture".

But before Canadians start packing their bags - "associate member" status does not currently exist within the EU and could take years to implement, given that all 27 EU member states would have to approve such an arrangement.

Nevertheless, people the BBC spoke to were excited about the potential prospect of working and studying in the EU as news of Carney's speech spread.

Alex Nash, from Montreal, said closer ties would clear away the obstacles of work visas and permits.

"It would certainly be really nice for that to be easier, more convenient and to be able to visit more easily," she said.

One person on a Facebook group, A Canadian Outlook, said they would love the opportunity for their grandchildren to study at European universities for better rates. Another woman said it would make it much easier for the home she already owns in France.

"Snow birds are going to love it," another person said, referring to Canadians who head to warmer locations for winter.

The sentiments hint at dissatisfaction in Canada over bilateral tensions with the US.

Growing up in Canada, David Jardine thought of the US as not just a neighbour, but an epicentre of culture and cool.

"I remember wanting to go and visit New York all the time," he told the BBC after finishing his overnight shift, not far from one of Toronto's most iconic buildings, the CN tower.

But he's become a lot more sceptical in the light of US President Donald Trump's trade war with Canada and rhetoric about annexation.

"I would say I think not only does it make more sense to associate closely with Europe, it's a place that I would rather be associating with given the way things are these days," he said.

Maggie Stainton, who manages local pub C'est What in Toronto's St Lawrence Market district, became emotional when she spoke about Canada's frayed ties with the US.

"It's too volatile with the United States," she said. "I feel that there's some stability in...
body.zh: 米里亚姆·莱文-戈尔德（Miriam Levin-Gold）喜欢马克·卡尼总理的想法，即加拿大人能够在与欧盟建立更密切关系的情况下在欧盟生活和工作。 这位通勤者在多伦多告诉英国广播公司：“我认为这对于年轻人探索世界不同的地方、在不同的地方工作并获得不同的经历来说是件好事。” 周四早上，加拿大人一觉醒来就听到了卡尼在斯特拉斯堡欧洲议会发表讲话的消息，他对欧盟希望加拿大成为其第一个“准成员”的雄心表示欢迎，同时他敦促在国防和能源方面进行更密切的合作。 总理说：“我们应该深化两国人民之间的联系，让我们的年轻人能够在大西洋两岸他们想要的地方生活、工作和学习。” 卡尼告诉欧洲议会议员，面对“地缘政治破裂”，加拿大和欧洲“在一起更强大”。 但在加拿大人开始收拾行李之前，欧盟目前并不存在“准成员”地位，而且可能需要数年时间才能实施，因为这种安排必须得到所有 27 个欧盟成员国的批准。 尽管如此，随着卡尼演讲的消息传开，接受英国广播公司采访的人们对在欧盟工作和学习的潜在前景感到兴奋。 来自蒙特利尔的亚历克斯·纳什表示，更紧密的联系将消除工作签证和许可证的障碍。 她说：“如果能更轻松、更方便、更轻松地参观，那就太好了。” Facebook 群组“加拿大展望”中的一位人士表示，他们希望自己的孙子有机会以更优惠的价格在欧洲大学学习。另一位女士表示，这将使她在法国已有的房屋变得更加容易。 另一位人士说：“雪鸟会喜欢这里的。”他指的是前往温暖地区过冬的加拿大人。 这种情绪暗示加拿大对与美国的双边紧张关系感到不满。 大卫·贾丁（David Jardine）在加拿大长大，他认为美国不仅是一个邻居，而且是文化和时尚的中心。 “我记得一直想去纽约看看，”他在结束夜班后告诉英国广播公司，那里距离多伦多最具标志性的建筑之一——加拿大国家电视塔不远。 但鉴于美国总统唐纳德·特朗普与加拿大的贸易战以及有关吞并的言论，他变得更加怀疑。 他说：“我想说，我认为与欧洲密切联系不仅更有意义，而且鉴于目前的情况，我更愿意与欧洲建立联系。” 玛吉·斯坦顿 (Maggie Stainton) 是多伦多圣劳伦斯市场区当地酒吧 C'est What 的老板，当她谈到加拿大与美国的紧张关系时，她变得情绪激动。 “美国的局势太不稳定了，”她说。 “我觉得有一定的稳定性......

reflection.en: The desire to explore, work, and study abroad speaks to a deep human longing for growth and new experiences. Colossians 3:23 reminds us that whatever we do, whether in our home country or in a new land, should be done with dedication, as if working for a higher purpose. This principle can guide individuals as they seek opportunities for personal and...
reflection.zh: 渴望在国外探索、工作和学习，反映了人类对成长和新体验的深切渴望。歌罗西书3章23节提醒我们，无论做什么，无论是在自己的国家还是在新地方，都应尽心竭力，好像是为主而做。这一原则可以指导个人在跨越国界寻求个人和职业发展机会时。

verse.textEn: Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for Yahweh, not for human masters.
verse.textZh: 无论做什么，都要从心里做，像是给主做的，不是给人做的。

title.en: Does the sight of small holes make you feel ill? There's a reason for that
title.zh: 看到小孔让你感到不适吗？原因就在这里

summary.en: Trypophobia, a well-known aversion to small holes or circular patterns, is having a viral moment on social media.
summary.zh: 恐穴症，一种对小孔或圆形图案的普遍厌恶，正在社交媒体上走红。

body.en:
Imagine you’re scrolling through TikTok and come across an image of a lotus seed pod or sponge.

You might not think much about it, but some people instantly feel sick. Their skin crawls, they feel nauseous, disgusted or very uncomfortable, and quickly swipe away.

This reaction is known as trypophobia, an aversion to clusters of holes or circular patterns.

About one in six people have at least some degree of discomfort when seeing these patterns.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Despite the "phobia" in its name, trypophobia is not simply a "fear of holes". It is also not recognised as a standalone mental health disorder. Unlike many phobias, disgust (rather than fear) is often the more dominant emotion.

Common triggers are lotus seed pods and honeycomb, or even everyday objects such as sponges, crumpets, bubbles, aerated chocolate or strawberries.

For most people with trypophobia these reactions are mild and can include disgust, nausea, skin crawling sensation, fear and anxiety.

But for a small group, symptoms can become so distressing they lead to people avoiding particular images, objects, or situations. This is a level of avoidance usually seen in specific phobias, such as arachnophobia, a fear of spiders.

In my own research, some participants avoided strawberries, cooking or baking, clothing, and even showers because of trypophobia-related triggers. These examples show trypophobia can sometimes significantly affect a person’s life.

The short answer is social media. Media stories, TikTok videos and online communities helped make trypophobia mainstream.

Shared images are often digitally altered to maximise discomfort and provoke strong reactions.

Research also suggests social media might influence how people experience trypophobia. For instance, in one 2024 study, almost two-thirds of people heard about it through social media. Those who had previously heard of trypophobia reported stronger reactions than those who had not.

But that doesn’t mean social media created trypophobia. Around one-quarter of people with trypophobia in the same study had never heard of it. Social media might increase awareness, but it cannot explain why some people react so strongly in the first place.

Scientists still debate why trypophobia exists, with two leading explanations emerging.

The first is the threat-detection theory. Some researchers argue trypophobic images resemble patterns found on poisonous or dangerous animals, such as snakes. According to this theory, humans might have evolved to react negatively to these visual cues because they can signal danger.

The second theory focuses on avoiding disease, with support from...
body.zh: 想象一下，您正在浏览 TikTok，并看到一张莲蓬或海绵的图片。 你可能没有多想，但有些人立刻就感到恶心。他们的皮肤会起鸡皮疙瘩，感到恶心、厌恶或非常不舒服，然后迅速消失。 这种反应被称为密集恐惧症，即对成群的孔或圆形图案的厌恶。 大约六分之一的人在看到这些图案时至少会感到某种程度的不适。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 尽管名字中有“恐惧症”，但密集恐惧症并不是简单的“对洞的恐惧”。它也不被认为是一种独立的精神健康障碍。与许多恐惧症不同，厌恶（而不是恐惧）通常是更主导的情绪。 常见的诱因是莲子荚和蜂窝，甚至是海绵、烤饼、气泡、充气巧克力或草莓等日常用品。 对于大多数患有密集恐惧症的人来说，这些反应是轻微的，可能包括恶心、恶心、皮肤爬行感、恐惧和焦虑。 但对于一小部分人来说，症状可能会变得非常令人痛苦，导致人们回避特定的图像、物体或情况。这是一种常见于特定恐惧症的回避程度，例如蜘蛛恐惧症，即对蜘蛛的恐惧。 在我自己的研究中，一些参与者由于密集恐惧症相关的诱因而避免吃草莓、做饭或烘烤、穿衣服，甚至洗澡。这些例子表明，密集恐惧症有时会严重影响一个人的生活。 简短的答案是社交媒体。媒体报道、TikTok 视频和在线社区帮助密集恐惧症成为主流。 共享的图像通常会经过数字修改，以最大程度地增加不适感并引起强烈反应。 研究还表明，社交媒体可能会影响人们经历密集恐惧症的方式。例如，在 2024 年的一项研究中，近三分之二的人是通过社交媒体听说的。那些以前听说过密集恐惧症的人比那些没有听说过的人反应更强烈。 但这并不意味着社交媒体造成了密集恐惧症。在同一项研究中，大约四分之一的密集恐惧症患者从未听说过它。社交媒体可能会提高人们的认识，但它无法解释为什么有些人一开始反应如此强烈。 科学家们仍在争论密集恐惧症为何存在，目前有两种主要解释。 第一个是威胁检测理论。一些研究人员认为，密集恐惧症图像类似于有毒或危险动物（例如蛇）上发现的图案。根据这一理论，人类可能已经进化到对这些视觉线索做出负面反应，因为它们可以发出危险信号。 第二个理论侧重于避免疾病，并得到......的支持。

reflection.en: Scrolling through social media can expose us to a barrage of images and ideas, some of which can trigger unexpected discomfort. Philippians 4:8 encourages us to intentionally focus our minds on what is true, noble, right, pure, lovely, admirable, excellent, and praiseworthy. This practice can help us navigate the digital world with greater peace and...
reflection.zh: 在社交媒体上浏览时，我们可能会接触到大量图像和想法，其中一些会引发意想不到的不适。腓立比书 4:8 鼓励我们有意识地将心思意念集中在真实、可敬、公义、清洁、可爱、有美名的事上，以及一切美德和值得称赞的事。这种操练可以帮助我们在数字世界中以更大的平安和分辨力前行，选择专注于滋养我们的思想，而非困扰我们的思想。

verse.textEn: Whatever is true, whatever is noble, whatever is right, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is admirable — think about such things.
verse.textZh: 凡是真实的、可敬的、公义的、清洁的、可爱的、有美名的，这些事你们都要思念。

title.en: This Olympic river has 500 crocodiles in it - but that's not the main concern
title.zh: 这条奥运河流有 500 条鳄鱼——但这并非主要担忧

summary.en: The Fitzroy River in Queensland, Australia, has been chosen as the venue for the 2032 Olympic rowing and canoe sprint events. Despite concerns about the river's inhabitants, including 500 crocodiles, the course has passed a technical assessment and been deemed safe for athletes.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚昆士兰州的菲茨罗伊河已被选为 2032 年奥运会赛艇和皮划艇冲刺项目的比赛场地。尽管人们对河中栖息着约 500 条鳄鱼感到担忧，但该赛道已通过技术评估，并被认定对运动员是安全和公平的。

body.en:
The annual rowing regatta for schools in the Australian state of Queensland usually passes off without too much attention.

Each year more than 600 of the state's most promising teenage rowers battle it out on the crocodile-inhabited Fitzroy River, in the city of Rockhampton.

"We've never had any media wanting to attend here," Anthea O'Loughlin, head of Rowing Queensland, tells the BBC.

But this year is different. In six years' time, the 2032 Brisbane Olympics and Paralympics are set to stage rowing and canoe sprint events in this very stretch of water, which has just passed a technical assessment and been endorsed as safe and fair for athletes.

While sightings of saltwater crocodiles on the river – which number around 500 and can grow to four metres (13ft) long – are not uncommon, state government files going back more than 40 years record no attacks by the reptiles on humans.

And while influential figures at last month's World Rowing congress in Amsterdam made occasional references to "safety", the presence of the reptiles was not their chief concern.

"Fairness" is what's been raised with British Rowing's chief executive Tom Solesbury – a reference to the tidal river's natural bends and currents, which many in the rowing community say make it unsuitable for elite competition.

Drew Ginn, who has won three Olympic gold medals for Australia in rowing, told BBC Radio he had concerns over potential flooding and "fairness and integrity" at the venue.

"Personally, I'm not fearful of the Australian animals but I've never had a crocodile near me," he said.

"I'm sure I'd row faster, I'm sure all the athletes would row faster. That's on the list of concerns, I don't think it's the highest priority in concerns but it was certainly cited very early on."

The German rowing body's president Moritz Petri said athletes had also questioned the sustainability of holding the event some 600km (373 miles) from Brisbane.

But the "so-called impediments" got short shrift from the most senior politician in Queensland, state premier David Crisafulli, who reached for less diplomatic language.

"Let's be honest, let's scratch beneath the surface and call it for what it is," he said days after the Amsterdam meeting.

"It is a group of interstate and overseas elites who are trying to bully their way because they don't want to go to regional Queensland and that's not right."

Rowing chiefs contacted by the BBC before Thursday's decision declined to comment directly on Crisafulli's "elites" remarks.

But both Petri and Simon Wickham, chief executive of Rowing New Zealand, said their concerns had nothing to do with regional or urban preference but with competitors getting fair racing.

Petri added it was about what's best for their athletes who will train four years for...
body.zh: 澳大利亚昆士兰州学校一年一度的赛艇比赛通常不会引起太多关注。 每年，该州 600 多名最有前途的青少年赛艇运动员都会在鳄鱼栖息的罗克汉普顿市菲茨罗伊河上展开角逐。 昆士兰赛艇协会负责人安西娅·奥洛林 (Anthea O'Loughlin) 告诉英国广播公司 (BBC)，“从来没有任何媒体愿意参加这里。” 但今年有所不同。六年后，2032 年布里斯班奥运会和残奥会将在这片刚刚通过技术评估并被认为对运动员安全、公平的水域举办赛艇和皮划艇短跑比赛。 虽然河上出现的咸水鳄鱼数量约 500 条，长度可达 4 米（13 英尺），这种情况并不少见，但 40 多年前的州政府文件没有记录这些爬行动物袭击人类的记录。 尽管上个月在阿姆斯特丹举行的世界赛艇大会上有影响力的人物偶尔提到“安全”，但爬行动物的存在并不是他们主要关心的问题。 英国赛艇协会首席执行官汤姆·索尔斯伯里提出的“公平”指的是潮汐河的自然弯曲和水流，许多赛艇界人士表示，这使其不适合精英比赛。 为澳大利亚赢得三枚奥运会赛艇金牌的德鲁·吉恩 (Drew Ginn) 告诉 BBC 电台，他对可能发生的洪水以及场馆的“公平和诚信”感到担忧。 “就我个人而言，我并不害怕澳大利亚的动物，但我附近从未有过鳄鱼，”他说。 “我确信我会划得更快，我确信所有运动员都会划得更快。这在担忧清单上，我不认为这是最优先考虑的问题，但它肯定很早就被引用了。” 德国赛艇协会主席莫里茨·佩特里表示，运动员们还质疑在距离布里斯班约 600 公里（373 英里）处举办赛事的可持续性。 但昆士兰州最高级别政治家、州州长戴维·克里萨富利(David Crisafulli)对这些“所谓的障碍”不屑一顾，他使用了不那么外交的语言。 “说实话，让我们深入了解它的本质，”他在阿姆斯特丹会议几天后说道。 “这是一群州际和海外精英试图欺凌他们的方式，因为他们不想去昆士兰地区，这是不对的。” 在周四的决定之前，英国广播公司联系的赛艇负责人拒绝直接对克里萨富利的“精英”言论发表评论。 但新西兰赛艇协会首席执行官佩特里和西蒙·威克姆均表示，他们的担忧与地区或城市偏好无关，而是与参赛者获得公平比赛有关。 佩特里补充说，这是关于什么对他们的运动员来说是最好的，他们将训练四年......

reflection.en: The Fitzroy River, home to 500 crocodiles, is set to host the 2032 Olympic rowing and canoe sprint events. This news brings to mind the dedication and discipline required for athletic competition, reminding us that even in challenging environments, human endeavor can strive for excellence. May athletes and organizers approach this unique venue with both...
reflection.zh: 拥有 500 条鳄鱼的菲茨罗伊河将成为 2032 年奥运会赛艇和皮划艇冲刺项目的举办地。这一消息令人联想到竞技体育所需的奉献和纪律，提醒我们即使在充满挑战的环境中，人类的努力也能追求卓越。愿运动员和组织者在以尊重其野生居民的态度来对待这个独特的场地时，也能秉持公平竞赛的精神。

verse.textEn: Do you not know that in a race all the runners run, but only one gets the prize? Run in such a way as to get the prize.
verse.textZh: 岂不知在场上赛跑的都跑，但得奖赏的只有一人？你们也当这样跑，好叫你们得着奖赏。

title.en: Russian birth tourism to Brazil increases
title.zh: 俄罗斯生育旅游涌向巴西

summary.en: An increasing number of Russians are traveling to Brazil to give birth, a trend that has grown since Russia's invasion of Ukraine and stricter regulations in Argentina. Children born in Brazil automatically receive Brazilian nationality, offering a pathway to citizenship for Russian families.
summary.zh: 自俄罗斯全面入侵乌克兰以及阿根廷收紧规定以来，越来越多的俄罗斯人选择前往巴西生育，他们的孩子将获得巴西国籍。

body.en:
Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and stricter regulations in Argentina, more and more Russians are choosing to travel to Brazil to give birth to children, who will obtain Brazilian nationality.

Yulia and Dmitri (whose names have been changed for reasons of safety) flew from Russia to Brazil this summer so that their child could be born there. Yulia was 32 weeks pregnant at the time of travel.

"Of course, we didn't say that I was pregnant at border control," Yulia told DW.

Her daughter was born at a private clinic in Santos, a city in southern Brazil. Anybody born in the country has an automatic right to Brazilian nationality. The family is currently preparing all the paperwork.

"We've achieved our minimum goal," said Dmitri. "With a Brazilian passport, our daughter will be able to travel without a visa to almost any country in the world. She won't have to apply for an expensive and time-consuming Schengen visa. We want her to be able to decide for herself where she studies, works or lives."

He said that a colleague of his had traveled to Brazil in early August with his pregnant wife for the same reasons.

Yulia and Dmitri said that they had spent the equivalent of about €10,000 (about $11,500) during the first six weeks of their stay in Brazil, which included the costs for several days of treatment for their daughter in intensive care. Dmitri quit his job at a bank for the trip and hopes to find work again after the family returns to their home in the Russian capital Moscow.

However, they are only planning to return once all the documents for their daughter are ready and that could take months. Other Russian families have decided to stay in Brazil permanently.

According to organizations and lawyers that provide support to Russians in Brazil, there has been an increase in immigration from Russia, particularly since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 , after which visa requirements for Russian nationals entering certain countries were tightened.

Birth tourism to Brazil has also increased since Argentina , which used to be one of the main destinations for people wanting their children to be born in a country that automatically grants citizenship to newborns, tightened its regulations. People who want their children to obtain Argentinian citizenship now have to have resided in Argentina for at least two years. Since 2025, the access of people who do not have a permanent residence permit to free healthcare has also been restricted.

According to the Russian news outlet RBC, more than 7,000 Russians applied for a residence permit in Argentina in 2023. By mid-2025, the number had decreased to about 1,800.

Meanwhile, almost 500 Brazilian passports were issued to Russians in 2024 and more than 600 the following year. More...
body.zh: 自俄罗斯全面入侵乌克兰以及阿根廷监管收紧以来，越来越多的俄罗斯人选择前往巴西生子，并获得巴西国籍。 尤利娅和德米特里（出于安全原因，化名）今年夏天从俄罗斯飞往巴西，以便他们的孩子在那里出生。旅行时尤利娅已怀孕 32 周。 “当然，我们并没有在边境管制时说我怀孕了，”尤利娅告诉德国之声。 她的女儿出生在巴西南部城市桑托斯的一家私人诊所。任何在该国出生的人都自动享有巴西国籍的权利。目前，家人正在准备所有文件。 “我们已经实现了最低目标，”德米特里说。 “有了巴西护照，我们的女儿将能够免签证前往世界上几乎任何国家。她不必申请昂贵且耗时的申根签证。我们希望她能够自己决定在哪里学习、工作或生活。” 他说，他的一位同事出于同样的原因，于八月初带着怀孕的妻子前往巴西。 尤利娅和德米特里说，他们在巴西逗留的前六周内花费了约10,000欧元（约11,500美元），其中包括女儿在重症监护室几天的治疗费用。德米特里为了这次旅行辞去了在银行的工作，并希望在全家返回俄罗斯首都莫斯科的家后再次找到工作。 然而，他们只计划在女儿的所有文件准备好后返回，这可能需要几个月的时间。其他俄罗斯家庭已决定永久留在巴西。 据为巴西俄罗斯人提供支持的组织和律师称，来自俄罗斯的移民数量有所增加，特别是自2022年俄罗斯全面入侵乌克兰以来，俄罗斯公民进入某些国家的签证要求收紧。 阿根廷曾是希望孩子在自动授予新生儿公民身份的国家出生的人们的主要目的地之一，但自从阿根廷收紧了法规以来，前往巴西的生育旅游也有所增加。现在，希望孩子获得阿根廷公民身份的人必须在阿根廷居住至少两年。自2025年起，没有永久居留许可的人获得免费医疗服务也受到限制。 据俄罗斯新闻媒体RBC报道，2023年有超过7000名俄罗斯人在阿根廷申请居留许可。到2025年中期，这一数字已减少至约1800人。 与此同时，2024 年向俄罗斯人发放了近 500 本巴西护照，次年又发放了 600 多本。更多的...

reflection.en: The desire for security and a better future for one's children is a powerful human drive. This news highlights how families navigate complex global circumstances, seeking opportunities for their offspring. The Psalmist reminds us that children are a gift from Yahweh, a heritage to be cherished and protected, regardless of the borders they cross.
reflection.zh: 为子女寻求安全和更美好未来的愿望是一种强大的人类驱动力。这则新闻凸显了家庭如何在复杂的全球环境中穿梭，为后代寻求机会。诗人提醒我们，子女是雅伟所赐的产业，是值得珍惜和保护的，无论他们跨越何种国界。

verse.textEn: Children are a heritage from Yahweh, offspring a reward from him.
verse.textZh: 儿女是雅伟所赐的产业。

title.en: Wife of US scholar jailed in China asks Trump to raise arrest at Xi meeting
title.zh: 被囚中国学者之妻请求特朗普在与习近平会晤时提及逮捕事件

summary.en: Sylvia Zin is among the family members of people imprisoned in China who are seeking Trump's help when he hosts the country's leader next week.
summary.zh: 西尔维娅·津是中国被监禁者的家属之一，她希望在下周美国总统特朗普接待中国领导人时获得他的帮助。

body.en:
The wife of a US scholar imprisoned in China on charges of spying and endangering national security has asked President Donald Trump to secure his release when he meets Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House next week.

U Min Zin, the director at a think tank focused on Myanmar, was arrested on 3 June after travelling to the Chinese city of Kunming for an academic conference.

"I'm deeply hopeful that President Trump will raise my husband's case with President Xi Jinping at the summit next week," his wife, Sylvia Zin, testified to Congress on Wednesday.

Xi is due to arrive for a state visit to Washington DC on Wednesday. It comes after Xi hosted Trump for a visit to Beijing in May.

Ahead of the meeting, families of prisoners being held in China have travelled to the US capital to advocate for their release.

Sylvia Zin appeared before the House Foreign Affairs Committee East Asia and Pacific Subcommittee on Wednesday for a hearing titled Lives, Not Leverage: The Long Arm of China and North Korea's Repression.

In her remarks, Zin said she believed Trump would also be able to secure the release of Chen Youlin, a US seismologist who tracks nuclear tests that has been held in prison in China for two years.

"Knowing the president's historic record on bringing wrongfully detained Americans home has reassured me that he will also be able to secure the swift release of Min Zin and other wrongfully detained citizens," she said.

Congresswoman Young Kim, the chairwoman of the subcommittee, opened the hearing by warning Americans: "If you travel to China, Beijing may take you hostage as leverage in diplomatic negotiation."

Speaking about Zin's arrest, she added: "Beijing wanted to send a message to those whose research inconvenienced it, and detained Mr Zin ahead of the upcoming Trump-Xi summit."

Min Zin, a student activist during Myanmar's 1988 pro-democracy movement, directs the Myanmar Institute for Strategic and Policy Studies (ISP-Myanmar), a think tank that studies China's role in Myanmar, including Chinese interests, relations, and regional influence.

The son of Hong Kong media mogul Jimmy Lai also appeared on Capitol Hill to call on Trump to secure his father's release. The US president previously raised the case with Xi, telling reporters that his Chinese counterpart "told me that would be a tough one".

Asked for comment on Thursday, a senior White House official, speaking anonymously, told the BBC: "Resolving the wrongful detentions of US citizens is always a top priority for the President."

Last month, the US State Department said that two Americans - U Min Zin and Chen Youlin - were being "wrongfully detained" in China.

This designation in the US allows the cases to be transferred to the office of the Special Envoy for Hostage...
body.zh: 一名因从事间谍活动和危害国家安全罪而在中国被监禁的美国学者的妻子要求唐纳德·特朗普总统下周在白宫会见中国国家主席习近平时确保释放他。 专注于缅甸的智库主任吴敏津 (U Min Zin) 于 6 月 3 日在前往中国昆明市参加学术会议后被捕。 “我非常希望特朗普总统能在下周的峰会上向习近平主席提出我丈夫的案件，”他的妻子西尔维娅·津周三在国会作证。 习近平将于周三抵达华盛顿特区进行国事访问。此前，习近平于五月接待了特朗普访问北京。 在会议召开之前，被关押在中国的囚犯家属已前往美国首都呼吁释放他们。 周三，西尔维娅·津 (Sylvia Zin) 出席众议院外交事务委员会东亚和太平洋小组委员会，参加题为“生命而非杠杆：中国的长臂与朝鲜镇压”的听证会。 辛在讲话中表示，她相信特朗普也能够确保美国地震学家陈友林获释，他跟踪核试验，已在中国监狱关押了两年。 她说：“了解总统将被错误拘留的美国人带回家的历史记录让我放心，他也将能够确保敏津和其他被错误拘留的公民迅速获释。” 该小组委员会主席、国会女议员 Young Kim 在听证会开始时警告美国人：“如果你前往中国，北京可能会将你扣为人质，作为外交谈判的筹码。” 谈到津先生的被捕，她补充道：“北京希望向那些对其研究造成不便的人传达一个信息，并在即将举行的特习峰会之前拘留了津先生。” 敏津 (Min Zin) 是 1988 年缅甸民主运动期间的一名学生活动家，领导着缅甸战略与政策研究所 (ISP-Myanmar)，该研究所是一个研究中国在缅甸的角色，包括中国利益、关系和地区影响力的智库。 香港媒体大亨黎智英的儿子也出现在国会山呼吁特朗普确保父亲获释。这位美国总统此前曾向习近平提出过此事，他告诉记者，中国总统“告诉我这将是一个艰难的问题”。 周四在被要求置评时，一位匿名的白宫高级官员告诉 BBC：“解决美国公民的错误拘留问题始终是总统的首要任务。” 上个月，美国国务院表示，两名美国人——吴敏津和陈又林——在中国被“错误拘留”。 美国的这一指定允许将案件转移到人质问题特使办公室......

reflection.en: Sylvia Zin is bravely speaking out, asking President Trump to raise the case of her imprisoned husband, U Min Zin, with President Xi Jinping. Her testimony to Congress is a powerful act of advocacy for someone silenced by imprisonment. This echoes the call to speak for those who cannot speak for themselves, ensuring their plight is not forgotten.
reflection.zh: 西尔维娅·津勇敢地发声，请求美国总统特朗普在与中国国家主席习近平会晤时提及她被监禁的丈夫乌敏津的案件。她向国会作证，是为一位被监禁而无法发声的人进行有力辩护。这呼应了为那些不能为自己发声的人说话的呼召，确保他们的困境不会被遗忘。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: A war-fatigued and anxious Russia picks a new parliament
title.zh: 饱受战争之苦、焦虑不安的俄罗斯迎来新议会

summary.en: Fuel shortages, drone strikes, and rumors of mobilization are increasing anxiety and war fatigue among Russians. As support for peace talks grows, the Kremlin is closely monitoring the situation ahead of parliamentary elections. Nearly half of those surveyed report a prevailing sense of alarm, and 60% believe the war...
summary.zh: 燃料短缺、无人机袭击和动员传言正在加剧俄罗斯民众的焦虑和战争疲劳。随着和平谈判的支持率不断上升，克里姆林宫在议会选举前密切关注着局势。近一半的受访者表示，普遍存在一种警惕感，60%的人认为乌克兰战争对他们的日常生活产生了负面影响。

body.en:
Fuel shortages, drone strikes and mobilization rumors are fueling anxiety and war fatigue in Russia. As support for peace talks grows among Russians, the Kremlin is watching closely ahead of parliamentary elections.

Russians are increasingly anxious . Nearly half of those surveyed by state pollster FOM say a sense of alarm is the prevailing mood among the people around them.

According to data by independent pollster ExtremeScan , 60% of Russians believe that the war against Ukraine has had negative consequences for their day-to-day lives. 

"Anxiety and war fatigue are driven by increasing uncertainty," Margarita Zavadskaya, a sociologist and senior research fellow at the Finnish Institute of International Affairs in Helsinki, told DW.

She says this year has seen a shift in public opinion. Rising prices, internet crackdowns, fuel shortages caused by Ukrainian strikes on oil refineries and rumors of another mobilization drive are making it harder for Russians to plan for the future. Some are even leaving the country, afraid they could be drafted after the elections.

Sociologist and the founder of ExtremeScan Elena Koneva said people were starting to ask the question: "How much does this war cost me and my family? And am I ready to pay this price? "

From September 18 to 20, Russians are voting for a new parliament (the State Duma) for the first time since 2022. It's the first parliamentary election to take place in Russia during the Ukraine war. And although there are unlikely to be any surprises in the official results, the Kremlin will be closely monitoring turnout.

"The Kremlin is confident it can fabricate whatever figures it needs. The question is how high of a price it will have to pay," said Zavadskaya.

Although elections in authoritarian systems like that of Russian President Vladimir Putin  have little to do with democratic change, they still serve an important purpose. They are a reality check on whether the population remains loyal. And for Putin, that is especially important right now.

"They are crucial for him because they demonstrate that the majority supports the main party, the party of war, and that he has legitimacy for further escalation and the continuation of this war," Russian opposition politician in exile Ilya Yashin told DW.

In the fifth year of the war in Ukraine, there is little sign the Kremlin is willing to end the conflict. United Russia, a party de facto led by Putin, is campaigning on a platform that lists victory in the war among its priorities. Its candidate list is headed by people presented as veterans of the war against Ukraine.

"The silent majority just wants the war to end," opposition politician Yulia Galyamina, who still lives in...
body.zh: 燃料短缺、无人机袭击和动员谣言正在加剧俄罗斯的焦虑和战争疲劳。随着俄罗斯人对和平谈判的支持不断增加，克里姆林宫正在议会选举前密切关注。 俄罗斯人越来越着急。国家民意调查机构 FOM 的调查显示，近一半的受访者表示，他们周围的人普遍存在一种恐慌感。 根据独立民意调查机构ExtremeScan的数据，60%的俄罗斯人认为针对乌克兰的战争给他们的日常生活带来了负面影响。 赫尔辛基芬兰国际事务研究所社会学家兼高级研究员玛格丽塔·扎瓦德斯卡娅 (Margarita Zavadskaya) 告诉德国之声：“日益增加的不确定性引发了焦虑和战争疲劳。” 她说今年公众舆论发生了转变。价格上涨、互联网打击、乌克兰炼油厂罢工造成的燃料短缺以及另一场动员活动的传言，都让俄罗斯人更难为未来做好计划。有些人甚至离开该国，担心选举后可能被征召入伍。 社会学家兼 ExtremeScan 创始人 Elena Koneva 表示，人们开始问这样一个问题：“这场战争让我和我的家人付出了多少代价？我准备好付出这个代价了吗？” 9 月 18 日至 20 日，俄罗斯民众将投票选出新议会（国家杜马），这是自 2022 年以来的首次。这是乌克兰战争期间俄罗斯举行的首次议会选举。 尽管官方结果不太可能出现任何意外，但克里姆林宫将密切关注投票率。 扎瓦德斯卡娅说：“克里姆林宫有信心能够捏造任何需要的数字。问题是它必须付出多大的代价。” 尽管像俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京这样的专制制度下的选举与民主变革关系不大，但它们仍然具有重要的目的。它们是对人们是否仍然忠诚的现实检验。 对于普京来说，这现在尤其重要。 俄罗斯流亡反对派政治家伊利亚·亚辛（Ilya Yashin）告诉德国之声：“这些对他来说至关重要，因为它们表明大多数人支持主要政党，即战争政党，并且他有进一步升级和继续这场战争的合法性。” 乌克兰战争已进入第五个年头，几乎没有迹象表明克里姆林宫愿意结束冲突。事实上由普京领导的统一俄罗斯党正在以赢得战争为首要任务的纲领进行竞选活动。其候选人名单中以对乌克兰战争的退伍军人为首。 “沉默的大多数只是希望战争结束，”反对派政治家尤利娅·加利亚米纳（Yulia Galyamina）仍然住在……

reflection.en: The pervasive anxiety and war fatigue described in Russia, with 60% of citizens feeling the negative impact of the conflict, speaks to a deep human longing for peace. Psalm 46:9 offers a vision of hope, stating that Yahweh will put an end to wars. This divine promise can be a source of comfort amidst the weariness and uncertainty felt by so many.
reflection.zh: 报道中描述的俄罗斯普遍存在的焦虑和战争疲劳，以及60%的公民感受到冲突的负面影响，这反映了人类对和平的深切渴望。《诗篇》46:9篇提供了一个充满希望的愿景，指出雅伟将止息战争。在如此多人感受到的疲惫和不确定中，这一神圣的应许可以成为一种安慰。

verse.textEn: He makes wars cease to the ends of the earth; he breaks the bow and shatters the spear.
verse.textZh: 他止息刀兵，直到地极；他折弓断枪。

title.en: Smuggling suspected as more rare animals seen in India
title.zh: 印度发现更多珍稀动物，疑似走私活动加剧

summary.en: Orangutans, rare reptiles, and other exotic animals are increasingly being found in India, suggesting the country is becoming a significant hub for trafficked wildlife. Recently, five infant orangutans, native to Indonesian islands, were discovered by rangers in India's Odisha state, prompting an inquiry from...
summary.zh: 红毛猩猩、稀有爬行动物和其他外来动物在印度日益增多，这表明该国正成为野生动物走私的重要目的地。最近，印度东部奥里萨邦的护林员在巴拉索尔地区发现五只幼年红毛猩猩，它们原产于印度尼西亚的岛屿，此发现已引起印度尼西亚林业部的关注。

body.en:
Orangutans, rare reptiles and other exotic animals are popping up in India, suggesting the country is becoming a major destination for trafficked wildlife.

Five infant orangutans, a species found only on the  Indonesian   island of Sumatra and on Borneo, were found in a forest by rangers patrolling in the Balasore district of India's eastern Odisha state last week.

Indonesia's Forestry Ministry has asked India to establish the origin of the abandoned orangutans, known for their shaggy red fur, and return them if they are found to have come from their usual habitat abroad.

The rescue of the rare apes has raised fresh questions about how exotic animals enter India and how the country is used in the illegal wildlife trade.

"The discovery on the eastern coast of India is a bit mind-boggling. It's like that time a few years ago when live kangaroos were found wandering along the highways of West Bengal," Kanitha Krishnasamy, Southeast Asia director at wildlife trade monitoring network TRAFFIC, told DW.

"What are orangutans doing in India? Were they smuggled from their native Malaysia or Indonesia or did they come from a facility?" she asked.

The Odisha government has asked the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau to investigate how the critically endangered animals reached the state. 

"These animals are not found in India and are mostly seen in the rainforests of Malaysia, Indonesia, Borneo and Sumatra in Southeast Asia," said Odisha's Forest and Environment Minister Ganesh Ram Singh Khuntia.

"We suspect that they might have been released in the Balasore district forest… by an international wildlife smuggling racket."

The orangutans are the latest in a series of exotic wildlife being seized in India.

In November 2024, authorities in the Indian city of Bengaluru seized 40 rare animals arriving from the Malaysian capital, Kuala Lumpur, including Aldabra giant tortoises, gibbons, American alligators and iguanas.

In June 2025, Mumbai Customs seized 284 exotic animals arriving in four consignments from the Thai capital, Bangkok, including snakes and tortoises.

In July 2025, customs officials in the Indian city of Pune intercepted 20 exotic animals from passengers arriving from Bangkok. They included 14 green tree pythons, four double-eyed fig parrots and two Sumatran striped rabbits. 

According to figures from TRAFFIC, 7,272 individual animals, alive and dead, were seized from passenger baggage in smuggling attempts between Thailand and India between January 2022 and May 2025, with more than 80% of interceptions taking place in India.

The animals included reptiles, birds and mammals — many apparently destined for the exotic pet trade.

"We have found hundreds of species and thousands of individuals being trafficked into India through...
body.zh: 红毛猩猩、稀有爬行动物和其他外来动物在印度不断出现，表明该国正在成为贩运野生动物的主要目的地。 上周，护林员在印度东部奥里萨邦巴拉索尔地区巡逻时，在森林中发现了五只仅在印度尼西亚苏门答腊岛和婆罗洲发现的猩猩幼崽。 印度尼西亚林业部已要求印度确定这些被遗弃的猩猩的来源，如果发现它们来自国外的惯常栖息地，则将其归还。这些猩猩以其蓬松的红色皮毛而闻名。 对稀有猿类的救援引发了新的问题：外来动物如何进入印度以及该国如何被用于非法野生动物贸易。 “印度东海岸的这一发现有点令人难以置信。就像几年前在西孟加拉邦的高速公路上发现活袋鼠一样，”野生动物贸易监测网络TRAFFIC东南亚主任Kanitha Krishnasamy告诉德国之声。 “猩猩在印度做什么？它们是从家乡马来西亚或印度尼西亚走私来的，还是来自某个设施？”她问道。 奥里萨邦政府已要求野生动物犯罪控制局调查这些极度濒危动物是如何到达该州的。 奥里萨邦森林和环境部长加内什·拉姆·辛格·昆蒂亚 (Ganesh Ram Singh Khuntia) 表示：“这些动物在印度没有发现，主要出现在马来西亚、印度尼西亚、婆罗洲和东南亚苏门答腊岛的雨林中。” “我们怀疑它们可能是被国际野生动物走私团伙释放到巴拉索尔地区森林中的。” 这些猩猩是印度查获的一系列外来野生动物中最新的一种。 2024年11月，印度班加罗尔当局查获了从马来西亚首都吉隆坡运来的40只珍稀动物，包括亚达伯拉象龟、长臂猿、美洲短吻鳄和鬣蜥。 2025 年 6 月，孟买海关查获了从泰国首都曼谷运来的四批货物中的 284 只珍奇动物，其中包括蛇和乌龟。 2025 年 7 月，印度浦那市的海关官员从曼谷抵达的旅客中截获了 20 只珍奇动物。其中包括 14 条绿树蟒、四只双眼无花果鹦鹉和两只苏门答腊条纹兔。 根据 TRAFFIC 的数据，2022 年 1 月至 2025 年 5 月期间，在泰国和印度之间的走私活动中，从乘客行李中查获了 7,272 只活的和死的动物，其中超过 80% 的拦截发生在印度。 这些动物包括爬行动物、鸟类和哺乳动物——许多显然是注定要进行外来宠物贸易的。 “我们发现数百个物种和数千个个体通过......被贩运到印度。

reflection.en: The discovery of abandoned orangutans and other exotic animals in India points to a hidden trade that exploits vulnerable creatures. These animals, far from their natural homes, are voiceless victims of trafficking. We are called to speak for those who cannot speak for themselves, advocating for the protection of the innocent and the vulnerable, whether...
reflection.zh: 在印度发现被遗弃的红毛猩猩和其他外来动物，揭示了一个剥削弱势生物的隐秘交易。这些动物远离家园，是走私案中无声的受害者。我们蒙召要为那些不能为自己发声的生命说话，倡导保护无辜和弱势者，无论他们是人还是动物。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Fact check: How disinformation fuels Houthi-Saudi conflict
title.zh: 事实核查：虚假信息如何助长胡塞武装与沙特冲突

summary.en: As fighting between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia escalates, old and repurposed videos have flooded social media, with many presented as fresh footage from the front lines.
summary.zh: 随着胡塞武装与沙特阿拉伯之间战事的升级，旧的及被重新利用的视频充斥社交媒体，许多被当作来自前线的最新画面。

body.en:
As fighting between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia escalates, old and repurposed videos have flooded social media, with many presented as fresh footage from the front lines.

The conflict between Yemen's Houthi  rebels and Saudi Arabia has sharply escalated in recent days, with Houthi forces making rapid gains along the Red Sea coast and taking control of key areas around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

Saudi Arabia has responded  with airstrikes. Houthi forces have launched drones and missiles towards Saudi territory . The renewed fighting has also raised concerns about global trade  via the Red Sea .

The conflict has also spread online, where significant disinformation has circulated.

DW's fact-checking team examined what is circulating and why a conflict that is so hard to observe independently leaves so much room for this kind of disinformation.

One nine-second clip has gone viral. It shows a huge explosion between buildings, with fireballs and screaming in the background.

Claim: A user posted the video on X with the Arabic caption "Yemeni forces are carrying out the strongest strikes in various areas in Saudi Arabia, including Abha." The video has more than 340,000 views. 

It was also posted in other languages , falsely claiming that it showed real footage from the current fighting.

The video is not only old, but also artificially generated. There are several visual clues in the clip such as the pattern of the explosions and the uniform way the smoke spreads.

A large-scale explosion of this kind would also have generated a very bright flash, and nearby buildings would likely have collapsed or at least had their windows shattered. Neither appears to have happened. 

One can also see, in the final seconds of the video, how a lamppost appears out of nowhere in the middle of the frame.

The audio is mostly unintelligible, but the speaker's tone does not appear to change after the huge explosion. Such a large explosion would normally be expected to trigger some audible reaction in the speaker's voice. 

On the technical side, Hive Moderation's AI detection analysis also confirmed that the video was artificially generated.

The very same video was shared  this June , then claiming to show explosions in Iran, as we found with a reverse image search.

Hannah Porter has spent years researching fake news and disinformation in Yemen and the country's wider information environment. She says this has been happening for years.

"There is less international attention in Yemen than there might be in other conflicts around the world. And, because there is not sufficient attention paid to Yemen, I think that allows more space for disinformation to spread not only within Yemen and in...
body.zh: 随着胡塞武装和沙特阿拉伯之间的战斗升级，旧视频和重新调整用途的视频充斥着社交媒体，其中许多都是来自前线的新鲜镜头。 也门胡塞武装与沙特阿拉伯之间的冲突近日急剧升级，胡塞武装在红海沿岸迅速取得进展，并控制了曼德海峡周边的关键地区。 沙特阿拉伯以空袭作为回应。胡塞武装向沙特境内发射了无人机和导弹。新一轮的战斗也引发了人们对红海全球贸易的担忧。 冲突还在网上蔓延，大量虚假信息在网上传播。 德国之声的事实核查团队调查了正在流传的内容，以及为何如此难以独立观察的冲突为此类虚假信息留下了如此大的空间。 一段 9 秒的视频已经疯传。它显示建筑物之间发生巨大爆炸，背景中有火球和尖叫声。 声明：一名用户在 X 上发布了该视频，并附有阿拉伯语标题“也门军队正在沙特阿拉伯多个地区进行最猛烈的打击，其中包括艾卜哈。” 该视频的观看次数已超过 340,000 次。 它还以其他语言发布，错误地声称它显示了当前战斗的真实镜头。 该视频不仅年代久远，而且还是人工生成的。剪辑中有一些视觉线索，例如爆炸的模式和烟雾扩散的均匀方式。 这种大规模爆炸也会产生非常明亮的闪光，附近的建筑物可能会倒塌或至少窗户被震碎。两者似乎都没有发生。 人们还可以看到，在视频的最后几秒钟，一根灯柱是如何突然出现在画面中间的。 音频大多难以理解，但扬声器的音调在巨大爆炸后似乎没有变化。如此大的爆炸通常会在说话者的声音中引发一些可听见的反应。 在技​​术方面，Hive Moderation的AI检测分析也证实该视频是人工生成的。 今年 6 月分享了同一个视频，然后声称显示了伊朗的爆炸，正如我们通过反向图像搜索发现的那样。 汉娜·波特花了数年时间研究也门以及该国更广泛的信息环境中的假新闻和虚假信息。她说这种情况已经发生很多年了。 “与世界各地的其他冲突相比，也门受到的国际关注较少。而且，由于对也门的关注不够，我认为这为虚假信息的传播提供了更多的空间，不仅在也门内部，而且......

reflection.en: In times of conflict, the lines between truth and falsehood can become dangerously blurred. The spread of old or manipulated videos as current events fuels the flames of war, making reconciliation even harder. We are called to speak truth, to be discerning, and to resist the temptation to amplify what we know to be untrue, especially when it inflames hatred.
reflection.zh: 在冲突时期，真相与谎言之间的界限可能变得极其模糊。将旧的或被操纵的视频当作当前事件传播，只会火上浇油，使和解更加困难。我们被呼召要讲真话，要有辨别力，并抵制那些会煽动仇恨的虚假信息的传播，尤其是在我们明知其不实的情况下。

verse.textEn: Therefore each of you must put off falsehood and speak truthfully to your neighbor.
verse.textZh: 所以你们要弃绝谎言，各人与邻舍说实话。

title.en: The world relies on this hidden water buffer. A ‘super’ El Niño is coming
title.zh: 世界依赖这个隐藏的水库。“超级”厄尔尼诺现象即将来临

summary.en: A decade-long decline in freshwater reserves is raising concerns about future water security, with an unprecedented El Niño expected to exacerbate the trend.
summary.zh: 淡水储备连续十年下降，引发了对未来水资源安全的担忧，而前所未有的厄尔尼诺现象预计将加剧这一趋势。

body.en:
The planet's water cycle is becoming increasingly erratic, swinging between too little and too much, the United Nations has warned, with an unprecedented El Niño expected to exacerbate the long-term trend.

Last year was among the driest for the world's rivers in over three decades, the UN's World Meteorological Organization (WMO) said in a report.

In 2025 — one of the warmest years on record — glaciers also shrank across all regions, even as groundwater levels in many parts of the world are in multi-year decline, it found.

Overall, the WMO's annual State of Global Water Resources report showed that Earth's freshwater storage — the total amount of water stored in groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, vegetation, and ice and snow — continued its decade-long decline.

Some elements of the water cycle change rapidly — like precipitation, river flow and soil moisture, responding to weather within days or weeks.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

WMO secretary-general Celeste Saulo voiced particular concern about the decline in "slow reserves", like groundwater and glaciers, which she said had traditionally served as the planet's "savings account".

They have served as "a buffer that absorbs bad years so that a single drought or a single dry season does not translate directly into a water crisis", she told reporters.

Now, "we are depleting that savings account", she warned. "We are spending our reserves."

Glaciers have also been shrinking at a precipitous rate, with 2025 marking the fourth consecutive year when they shed significant ice mass across all regions.

Between 2023 and 2025, the report estimated that glaciers lost a cumulative global glacier mass of 1,400 gigatonnes of water — roughly equal to the water required to fill 560 million Olympic-sized swimming pools, or about a third of the world's annual freshwater withdrawals.

"Groundwater tells a similar story: nearly two-thirds of monitored wells worldwide showed conditions outside the historical norm in 2025," Saulo said.

She highlighted that this was happening in parallel with "more water-related disasters".

In particular, she pointed to the current El Niño pattern, which is expected to be the strongest since comparable records began four decades ago.

El Niño is the warm phase of a natural climate cycle that occurs every two to seven years and is characterised by above-average sea surface temperatures across the Pacific, bringing worldwide changes in wind and rainfall patterns and erratic weather.

"The strengthening El Niño will increase the risk of drought in some areas, and flooding in others," Saulo...
body.zh: 联合国警告说，地球的水循环正变得越来越不稳定，在太少和太多之间摇摆，前所未有的厄尔尼诺现象预计将加剧这一长期趋势。 联合国世界气象组织（WMO）在一份报告中表示，去年是三十多年来世界河流最干旱的一年。 研究发现，2025 年是有记录以来最温暖的年份之一，尽管世界许多地区的地下水位多年来一直在下降，但所有地区的冰川都出现了萎缩。 总体而言，世界气象组织的年度全球水资源状况报告显示，地球的淡水储存量——地下水、湖泊和河流、土壤湿度、植被以及冰雪中储存的水总量——持续十年来的下降。 水循环的一些要素变化很快，比如降水、河流流量和土壤湿度，在几天或几周内就会对天气做出反应。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 世界气象组织秘书长塞莱斯特·索洛对地下水和冰川等“缓慢储备”的减少表示特别担忧，她说这些传统上一直是地球的“储蓄账户”。 她告诉记者，它们起到了“吸收糟糕年份的缓冲作用，这样一次干旱或一次旱季就不会直接转化为水危机”。 她警告说，现在“我们正在耗尽储蓄账户”。 “我们正在花费我们的储备。” 冰川也在急剧萎缩，到 2025 年，所有地区的冰川将连续第四年流失。 该报告估计，2023 年至 2025 年间，全球冰川累计流失了 1,400 十亿吨水，大约相当于填满 5.6 亿个奥运会规模的游泳池所需的水，约占世界每年淡水抽取量的三分之一。 “地下水讲述了一个类似的故事：到 2025 年，全球近三分之二的监测井的状况超出了历史正常水平，”Saulo 说。 她强调，这种情况与“更多与水有关的灾难”同时发生。 她特别指出了当前的厄尔尼诺现象，预计将是自四十年前有类似记录以来最强烈的一次。 厄尔尼诺现象是自然气候周期的温暖阶段，每两到七年发生一次，其特点是太平洋海面温度高于平均水平，带来全球风和降雨模式的变化以及不稳定的天气。 “厄尔尼诺现象的加强将增加一些地区发生干旱和其他地区发生洪水的风险，”索洛...

reflection.en: The UN's report on dwindling freshwater reserves and an erratic water cycle paints a stark picture of our planet's vulnerability. As we face the prospect of a 'super' El Niño, the news reminds us that the Earth's resources are not ours to deplete indefinitely. Psalm 24:1 declares, 'The earth is Yahweh's, and everything in it.' This truth calls us to...
reflection.zh: 联合国关于淡水储备减少和水循环不稳定的报告，描绘了一幅严峻的地球脆弱景象。当我们面对“超级”厄尔尼诺现象的可能来临时，这则新闻提醒我们，地球的资源并非可供我们无限消耗。诗篇24:1宣告：“地和其中所充满的，世界和居住在其中的，都属于雅伟。”这一真理呼唤我们负责任地管理托付给我们的水和所有受造之物。

verse.textEn: The earth is Yahweh's, and everything in it, the world, and all who live in it.
verse.textZh: 地和其中所充满的，世界和住在其间的，都属雅伟。

title.en: Ed Sheeran rarely talks politics. The Macklemore controversy has put him at the centre of it
title.zh: 埃德·希兰很少谈论政治。麦克尔莫尔的争议使他处于中心

summary.en: As artists quit Ed Sheeran's tour in solidarity with Macklemore, a wider debate is unfolding.
summary.zh: 随着艺术家们退出了埃德·希兰的巡演以声援麦克尔莫尔，一场更广泛的辩论正在展开。

body.en:
Ed Sheeran has built one of the world's biggest music careers while largely avoiding one of the more divisive parts of modern celebrity: politics.

The English singer has spoken publicly about some causes over the years, including performing at a major benefit concert for Ukraine following Russia's 2022 invasion. But he has generally resisted using his concerts as a political platform, something he says is deliberate.

Now, Macklemore's removal from his United States tour has drawn Sheeran into a political debate he has largely sought to avoid.

In less than two weeks, Macklemore has made a high-profile pro-Palestinian speech while opening for Sheeran, been removed from his remaining US tour dates, and been followed out the door by four other acts.

Sheeran has insisted the decision to remove the American rapper wasn't his and says he spent days trying to prevent it.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

But the fallout has nevertheless dragged the 35-year-old singer into a highly charged debate over the Israel-Gaza conflict, antisemitism and the role, or responsibility, of artists to use their platforms to take a political stand.

And it has forced Sheeran to publicly explain why, unlike Macklemore, he generally chooses not to.

"I have my personal views on this devastating conflict," Sheeran wrote in a lengthy statement posted to Instagram this week.

"Just because I choose not to speak publicly, it doesn't mean I don't have them, and it doesn't mean I don't care."

The dispute began on 4 September, when Macklemore was performing as a support act on Sheeran's Loop Tour at a New Jersey stadium.

Introducing his 2024 protest song Hind's Hall, the rapper told the crowd that part of the reason he wanted to join the tour was to use its enormous stadium audiences to amplify his support for Palestinians.

"A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very near and dear to my heart: 'Free Palestine'," Macklemore said.

The following day, he again addressed the conflict, telling Jewish members of the audience that his criticism of Israel was not criticism of them.

The remarks sparked a backlash, with the Israeli-American Council launching a petition calling for Macklemore to be removed from the tour, arguing Sheeran's stage should not be used for "one-sided political propaganda".

By Monday, he was off the tour. Promoter Messina Touring Group said venue owners hosting upcoming dates had indicated they would not allow shows featuring Macklemore to proceed.

The episode has highlighted the starkly different approaches the two artists take to their public...
body.zh: 艾德·希兰 (Ed Sheeran) 建立了世界上最大的音乐事业之一，同时在很大程度上避开了现代名人中最具争议性的部分之一：政治。 这位英国歌手多年来曾公开谈论过一些原因，包括在俄罗斯 2022 年入侵后为乌克兰举办的一场大型慈善音乐会上表演。但他总体上拒绝将音乐会作为政治平台，他说这是故意的。 现在，麦克莫尔被取消美国之行，这让希兰陷入了一场他在很大程度上试图避免的政治辩论。 在不到两周的时间里，麦克莫尔在为希兰开场时发表了高调的亲巴勒斯坦演讲，被从他剩余的美国巡演日期中删除，并被其他四位表演者追随出局。 希兰坚称，解雇这位美国说唱歌手的决定不是他自己做出的，并表示他花了几天时间试图阻止这一决定。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 但此事的后果却让这位 35 岁的歌手卷入了一场关于以色列-加沙冲突、反犹太主义以及艺术家利用自己的平台表明政治立场的角色或责任的激烈辩论。 这迫使希兰公开解释为什么与麦克莫尔不同，他通常选择不这样做。 “我对这场毁灭性的冲突有我个人的看法，”希兰在本周发布在 Instagram 上的一份长篇声明中写道。 “仅仅因为我选择不公开发言，并不意味着我没有它们，也不意味着我不在乎。” 这场纠纷始于 9 月 4 日，当时 Macklemore 在新泽西州体育场为 Sheeran's Loop Tour 表演助兴表演。 这位说唱歌手在介绍他的 2024 年抗议歌曲《Hind's Hall》时告诉观众，他想参加巡演的部分原因是利用体育场庞大的观众来扩大他对巴勒斯坦人的支持。 麦克勒莫尔说：“我最初想要参加这次巡演的一个重要原因是，我可以站在这样的体育场里，说出两个我心目中非常亲近的词：‘自由巴勒斯坦’。” 第二天，他再次谈到了这场冲突，告诉观众中的犹太成员，他对以色列的批评并不是对他们的批评。 这一言论引发了强烈反对，以色列-美国委员会发起请愿书，要求将麦克勒莫从巡演中除名，并认为希兰的舞台不应被用于“单方面的政治宣传”。 到了周一，他就退出了巡演。发起人 Messina Touring Group 表示，举办即将举行的演出的场地所有者已表示，他们不会允许麦克莫尔的演出继续进行。 这一集凸显了两位艺术家对公众采取的截然不同的方式......

reflection.en: Ed Sheeran has built a career on largely avoiding political statements, a deliberate choice to sidestep divisive issues. However, the controversy surrounding Macklemore's pro-Palestinian speech has unexpectedly placed Sheeran at the center of a political debate he sought to avoid. This situation highlights how even attempts to remain neutral can draw...
reflection.zh: 埃德·希兰的职业生涯很大程度上建立在避免政治表态之上，这是他刻意选择避开争议性问题的做法。然而，围绕麦克尔莫尔亲巴勒斯坦演讲的争议却出人意料地将希兰置于他试图回避的政治辩论的中心。这种情况凸显了即使是试图保持中立，也可能将个人卷入公众的争论之中，尤其是在个人信念与公众平台交织在一起时。

verse.textEn: Do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit. Rather, in humility value others above yourselves.
verse.textZh: 凡事不可结党，不可贪图虚浮的荣耀；只要存心谦卑，各人看别人比自己强。

title.en: Wife of US scholar jailed in China asks Trump to raise arrest at Xi meeting
title.zh: 被囚中国学者之妻请求特朗普在与习近平会晤时提及逮捕事件

summary.en: Sylvia Zin is among the family members of people imprisoned in China who are seeking Trump's help when he hosts the country's leader next week.
summary.zh: 西尔维娅·津是中国被监禁者的家属之一，她希望在下周美国总统特朗普接待中国领导人时获得他的帮助。

body.en:
The wife of a US scholar imprisoned in China on charges of spying and endangering national security has asked President Donald Trump to secure his release when he meets Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House next week.

U Min Zin, the director at a think tank focused on Myanmar, was arrested on 3 June after travelling to the Chinese city of Kunming for an academic conference.

"I'm deeply hopeful that President Trump will raise my husband's case with President Xi Jinping at the summit next week," his wife, Sylvia Zin, testified to Congress on Wednesday.

Xi is due to arrive for a state visit to Washington DC on Wednesday. It comes after Xi hosted Trump for a visit to Beijing in May.

Ahead of the meeting, families of prisoners being held in China have travelled to the US capital to advocate for their release.

Sylvia Zin appeared before the House Foreign Affairs Committee East Asia and Pacific Subcommittee on Wednesday for a hearing titled Lives, Not Leverage: The Long Arm of China and North Korea's Repression.

In her remarks, Zin said she believed Trump would also be able to secure the release of Chen Youlin, a US seismologist who tracks nuclear tests that has been held in prison in China for two years.

"Knowing the president's historic record on bringing wrongfully detained Americans home has reassured me that he will also be able to secure the swift release of Min Zin and other wrongfully detained citizens," she said.

Congresswoman Young Kim, the chairwoman of the subcommittee, opened the hearing by warning Americans: "If you travel to China, Beijing may take you hostage as leverage in diplomatic negotiation."

Speaking about Zin's arrest, she added: "Beijing wanted to send a message to those whose research inconvenienced it, and detained Mr Zin ahead of the upcoming Trump-Xi summit."

Min Zin, a student activist during Myanmar's 1988 pro-democracy movement, directs the Myanmar Institute for Strategic and Policy Studies (ISP-Myanmar), a think tank that studies China's role in Myanmar, including Chinese interests, relations, and regional influence.

The son of Hong Kong media mogul Jimmy Lai also appeared on Capitol Hill to call on Trump to secure his father's release. The US president previously raised the case with Xi, telling reporters that his Chinese counterpart "told me that would be a tough one".

Asked for comment on Thursday, a senior White House official, speaking anonymously, told the BBC: "Resolving the wrongful detentions of US citizens is always a top priority for the President."

Last month, the US State Department said that two Americans - U Min Zin and Chen Youlin - were being "wrongfully detained" in China.

This designation in the US allows the cases to be transferred to the office of the Special Envoy for Hostage...
body.zh: 一名因从事间谍活动和危害国家安全罪而在中国被监禁的美国学者的妻子要求唐纳德·特朗普总统下周在白宫会见中国国家主席习近平时确保释放他。 专注于缅甸的智库主任吴敏津 (U Min Zin) 于 6 月 3 日在前往中国昆明市参加学术会议后被捕。 “我非常希望特朗普总统能在下周的峰会上向习近平主席提出我丈夫的案件，”他的妻子西尔维娅·津周三在国会作证。 习近平将于周三抵达华盛顿特区进行国事访问。此前，习近平于五月接待了特朗普访问北京。 在会议召开之前，被关押在中国的囚犯家属已前往美国首都呼吁释放他们。 周三，西尔维娅·津 (Sylvia Zin) 出席众议院外交事务委员会东亚和太平洋小组委员会，参加题为“生命而非杠杆：中国的长臂与朝鲜镇压”的听证会。 辛在讲话中表示，她相信特朗普也能够确保美国地震学家陈友林获释，他跟踪核试验，已在中国监狱关押了两年。 她说：“了解总统将被错误拘留的美国人带回家的历史记录让我放心，他也将能够确保敏津和其他被错误拘留的公民迅速获释。” 该小组委员会主席、国会女议员 Young Kim 在听证会开始时警告美国人：“如果你前往中国，北京可能会将你扣为人质，作为外交谈判的筹码。” 谈到津先生的被捕，她补充道：“北京希望向那些对其研究造成不便的人传达一个信息，并在即将举行的特习峰会之前拘留了津先生。” 敏津 (Min Zin) 是 1988 年缅甸民主运动期间的一名学生活动家，领导着缅甸战略与政策研究所 (ISP-Myanmar)，该研究所是一个研究中国在缅甸的角色，包括中国利益、关系和地区影响力的智库。 香港媒体大亨黎智英的儿子也出现在国会山呼吁特朗普确保父亲获释。这位美国总统此前曾向习近平提出过此事，他告诉记者，中国总统“告诉我这将是一个艰难的问题”。 周四在被要求置评时，一位匿名的白宫高级官员告诉 BBC：“解决美国公民的错误拘留问题始终是总统的首要任务。” 上个月，美国国务院表示，两名美国人——吴敏津和陈又林——在中国被“错误拘留”。 美国的这一指定允许将案件转移到人质问题特使办公室......

reflection.en: Sylvia Zin is bravely speaking out, asking President Trump to raise the case of her imprisoned husband, U Min Zin, with President Xi Jinping. Her testimony to Congress is a powerful act of advocacy for someone silenced by imprisonment. This echoes the call to speak for those who cannot speak for themselves, ensuring their plight is not forgotten.
reflection.zh: 西尔维娅·津勇敢地发声，请求美国总统特朗普在与中国国家主席习近平会晤时提及她被监禁的丈夫乌敏津的案件。她向国会作证，是为一位被监禁而无法发声的人进行有力辩护。这呼应了为那些不能为自己发声的人说话的呼召，确保他们的困境不会被遗忘。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: The US government is failing Americans on AI | Shakeel Hashim

summary.en: The article criticizes the US government's approach to Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly the Republican stance favoring self-regulation by companies. It argues this is a dereliction of duty that increases AI risks. Prominent AI CEOs like Sam Altman, Elon Musk, and Dario Amodei have called for a slowdown due...

body.en: Trump and Republicans want companies to regulate themselves. It’s a dereliction of duty that will make AI less safe It is hard to get Sam Altman, Elon Musk and Dario Amodei to agree on much. But over the weekend, all three AI company CEOs called for AI development to slow down in the face of growing, alarming risks. Their employees are sounding the siren too, with one researcher publicly quitting and accusing OpenAI and Anthropic of “gambling with our lives”. The combination of dire warnings from insiders and growing real-world evidence of rogue AIs should, in a sane world, lead to government action. Instead, Donald Trump and the Republican leadership have their heads in the sand. Continue reading...
body.zh: 特朗普和共和党人希望企业自我监管。失职会让人工智能变得不那么安全萨姆·奥尔特曼、埃隆·马斯克和达里奥·阿莫迪很难在很多方面达成一致。但上周末，三位人工智能公司首席执行官都呼吁，面对不断增长的令人震惊的风险，放慢人工智能的发展速度。他们的员工也拉响了警报，一名研究人员公开辞职，并指责 OpenAI 和 Anthropic “拿我们的生命进行赌博”。在一个理智的世界里，内部人士发出的可怕警告和现实世界中越来越多的流氓人工智能证据相结合，应该会导致政府采取行动。相反，唐纳德·特朗普和共和党领导层却把头埋在沙子里。继续阅读...

Like metals tested in a furnace, the leaders and companies driving this technology are being tested by its potential and the praise it garners. The calls for caution from within the industry itself suggest a recognition that unchecked progress can lead to unforeseen...

title.en: An unexpected move by the US has sparked anger from China and Russia
title.zh: 美国出人意料的举动引发中俄愤怒

summary.en: Russia and China have expressed alarm at the revelation, warning against the idea of space becoming a "battlefield". The United States has confirmed for the first time that it has deployed weapons in space, a move that has sparked anger from China and Russia.
summary.zh: 俄罗斯和中国对这一消息表示震惊，警告太空可能成为“战场”。美国首次证实已在太空部署武器，此举引发了中国和俄罗斯的愤怒。

body.en:
The United States has confirmed for the first time that it has deployed weapons in space, a remarkable revelation after warnings about countries such as Russia possibly weaponising a global frontier long agreed in treaties to be used for only peaceful purposes.

US Air Force secretary Troy Meink said the US has fielded "on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending the Joint Force against hostile adversary action".

Meink did not detail what the weapons were, how they work or if they were targeting other objects in space or on Earth.

The US had warned two years ago that Russia was developing a new space-based, anti-satellite weapon, though the White House said the danger wasn't imminent at the time.

But reports of the anti-satellite weapon reflected longstanding worries about space threats from Russia and China, given that much US infrastructure is dependent on satellite communications. The US has also previously demonstrated its own abilities to shoot down satellites from Earth.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

In his remarks to the Air and Space Forces Association's Air, Space & Cyber Conference on Tuesday AEST, Meink also said the Air Force was adding more autonomous systems to its capabilities and predicted the service would look "radically different" by 2032.

For example, he foresaw one-way attack drones replacing artillery as the "primary killer".

Analysts said that the revelation by the US confirmed an open secret, but the timing of the announcement risked exacerbating tensions with China and the risk of a weapons race in space.

In 2019, during his first term, US President Donal Trump created the Space Force as a separate military branch. In his second term, he has announced the Golden Dome missile defence system, which includes plans to put US weapons in space.

Trump said last year that he expected the system would be "fully operational before the end of my term", which ends in January 2029.

He said the system would have the capability of intercepting missiles "even if they are launched from space".

Trump also directed the Pentagon to pursue the space-based interceptors in an executive order during the first week of his presidency.

The Congressional Budget Office estimated that just the space-based components of the Golden Dome could cost as much as US$542 billion ($760 billion) over the next 20 years.

For the US, both Russia and China — its two main geopolitical rivals — pose potential threats to US interests in space.

China "develops and operates space and counterspace capabilities as part of a military modernisation strategy," according to the US Space Force.

May wisdom guide nations to prioritize cooperation and shared stewardship of this...
