title.en: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund
title.zh: 尼泊尔将利用新的洪水研究，向联合国气候灾难基金索赔数百万美元

summary.en: A new study suggests climate change was a likely contributor to the massive flood that occurred on the Nepal-Tibet border last month. Nepal plans to use this study to request approximately $20 million from the UN Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage to aid those affected by the disaster, which has resulted in around...
summary.zh: 一项新研究表明，气候变化可能是上个月发生在尼泊尔-西藏边境的特大洪水的一个可能因素。尼泊尔计划利用这项研究，向联合国“损失与损害”基金申请约2000万美元，以援助受灾民众。此次灾难已造成约1400人死亡，超过6000人失踪。

body.en:
Nepal plans to use a new study linking climate change to the deadly floods last month as the basis of a financial request from a United Nations fund.

The BBC understands that Nepal hopes to claim around $20m (£15m) from the UN Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage, which helps countries affected by climate change.

Around 1,400 people have died in the disaster while 6,150 people remain missing in Nepal as of Wednesday, according official data.

The study by research group World Weather Attribution, published on Thursday, says climate change was a likely contributing factor in the avalanche of rock and ice that unleashed devastating floods on the Nepal-Tibet border last month.

There was "absolutely no doubt that human-induced climate change played a role here in the preconditioning of the disaster", said Dr Friederike Otto, an Imperial College London climatologist who co-authored the study.

Massive floods and landslides swept through border towns and villages in Nepal and Tibet, wiping out thousands of houses, destroying energy infrastructure and leaving thousands dead or missing.

Scientists say the floods were caused by a collapse of rock wall and glacier ice near the peak of Langtang Lirung, a mountain on Nepal's side of the Himalayas.

According to the study, July and August temperatures in the area were around 1.5C (2.7F) warmer "due to human influence on the climate".

Meanwhile, glaciers in the region had also been thinning by about half a metre (1.6ft) a year, which could weaken existing fractures and increase instability.

Heavy snowfall last October and November also added to a large amount of meltwater early this year.

Climate change, while not the only cause of the disaster, was a "destabilising factor acting on a pre-existing geological predisposition", the study said.

In the wake of the floods, Nepal's leaders have said the country needs around $5bn (£3.7bn) to rebuild itself.

The UN Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage, which came into operation last year, requires countries to submit evidence proving that the losses they faced were caused by climate change.

Nepali officials had been preparing satellite and drone images, as well as preliminary reports, to back up its request to the fund.

But the World Weather Attribution report is now the strongest evidence for their claim that climate change was a significant factor in the collapse of rock and ice at Langtang Lirung, authorities say.

The report "will be the main basis of our claim as it has detailed what role climate has played in this disaster," said Maheshwar Dhakal, spokesperson for Nepal's Ministry of Agriculture, Forest and Environment.

Nepali authorities have called for global efforts to tackle climate change, saying the country is one of the lowest contributors to...
body.zh: 尼泊尔计划利用一项将气候变化与上个月致命洪水联系起来的新研究作为向联合国基金提出财务请求的基础。 据BBC了解，尼泊尔希望向联合国应对损失和损害基金索要约2000万美元（1500万英镑），该基金旨在帮助受气候变化影响的国家。 根据官方数据，截至周三，尼泊尔已有约 1,400 人在这场灾难中丧生，另有 6,150 人失踪。 世界天气归因研究组织周四发表的这项研究称，气候变化可能是造成上个月尼泊尔-西藏边境发生毁灭性洪水的岩石和冰雪崩的一个因素。 该研究的合著者、伦敦帝国理工学院气候学家弗里德里克·奥托博士表示，“毫无疑问，人类引起的气候变化在这场灾难的预适应中发挥了作用”。 大规模洪水和山体滑坡席卷了尼泊尔和西藏的边境城镇和村庄，摧毁了数千所房屋，摧毁了能源基础设施，并造成数千人死亡或失踪。 科学家表示，洪水是由喜马拉雅山尼泊尔一侧的朗塘利隆山峰附近的岩壁和冰川崩塌引起的。 根据这项研究，“由于人类对气候的影响”，该地区 7 月和 8 月的气温升高了 1.5 摄氏度（2.7 华氏度）左右。 与此同时，该地区的冰川也以每年约半米（1.6英尺）的速度变薄，这可能会削弱现有的裂缝并增加不稳定性。 去年10月和11月的大雪也导致今年年初出现大量融水。 研究称，气候变化虽然不是造成这场灾难的唯一原因，但却是“作用于预先存在的地质倾向的不稳定因素”。 洪水过后，尼泊尔领导人表示，该国需要约 50 亿美元（37 亿英镑）进行重建。 去年投入运行的联合国应对损失和损害基金要求各国提交证据，证明其面临的损失是由气候变化造成的。 尼泊尔官员一直在准备卫星和无人机图像以及初步报告，以支持其向该基金提出的请求。 但当局表示，世界天气归因报告现在是最有力的证据，证明了他们的说法，即气候变化是导致 Langtang Lirung 岩石和冰崩塌的一个重要因素。 尼泊尔农业、森林和环境部发言人马赫什瓦尔·达卡尔（Maheshwar Dhakal）表示，这份报告“将成为我们主张的主要依据，因为它详细说明了气候在这场灾难中所扮演的角色”。 尼泊尔当局呼吁全球努力应对气候变化，并表示该国是对气候变化贡献最小的国家之一。

reflection.en: The earth groans under the weight of climate change, as evidenced by the devastating floods in Nepal. In times of such crisis, when natural forces seem overwhelming, Psalm 46:1 reminds us that Yahweh is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble. May this truth offer solace and a foundation for rebuilding amidst the devastation.
reflection.zh: 正如尼泊尔的毁灭性洪水所证明的那样，大地在气候变化的重压下呻吟。在这样的危机时刻，当自然力量似乎势不可挡时，《诗篇》46:1提醒我们，雅伟是我们的避难所和力量，是患难中随时的帮助。愿这个真理在毁灭中提供慰藉和重建的基础。

verse.textEn: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.
verse.textZh: 神是我们的避难所，是我们的力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。

title.en: The farmer who turned to singing after bovine TB silenced his fields
title.zh: 农民因牛结核病而失业，转而唱歌

summary.en: Dairy farmer Mervyn Kelso experienced profound sadness and emptiness after losing his entire herd to bovine TB. He found solace and a new path through joining a choir, which lifted his spirits and led to unexpected opportunities.
summary.zh: 奶牛养殖户 Mervyn Kelso 在因牛结核病失去整个牛群后，经历了巨大的悲伤和空虚。他通过加入合唱团找到了慰藉和新的生活方向，这提升了他的精神，并带来了意想不到的机会。

body.en:
When bovine TB led to the loss of his entire herd, dairy farmer Mervyn Kelso struggled with the sadness of the empty fields and the silence of the milking yard.

It was a traumatic time for a man who had farmed his whole life, and it was hard watching his neighbours tend to their cows.

His sister suggested he should join the Farmers' Choir and that turned out to be a "great lifter".

Fast forward four years, and Mervyn has sung for the King, met musical royalty and his choir is up for a national award.

Mervyn's first batch of cows were lost in November 2021. At the same time, a friend who had been around the County Antrim farm for three generations died.

Mervyn and his wife Ruth, who live near Portglenone, relied on their faith for "the strength to carry on".

Mervyn would sing in church and so when the Farmers' Choir restarted in nearby Ballymena that autumn, he decided to give it a go.

He said it had been rewarding and different - a relief to the tough challenges of day-to-day farming.

"Farming is one very lonely job, even more lonely than it was a generation ago, because labour is so difficult to get," he said.

"It has the effect of depressing you, and that's why being involved in such a thing as a choir or any social event outside farming is good for anyone."

"It was a hard time for both of us and the choir was definitely a great lifter," she said.

"It was just great to have something to lift us because you weren't busy on the farm - well, you did some extra odd jobs, but it wasn't like the usual level of busyness."

She said she has made "some lovely friends" and they get to see each other at choir rehearsals, concerts and céilís.

"Sometimes you see a different side of a choir member when you're not just sitting beside them singing, and that's really good, socially," she added.

He grew up on a dairy farm and remembers his father talking about people at harvest time, helping each other out then sharing "a bit of craic and banter".

He said the choir helped fill a social gap that has emerged in rural life as farming has become more automated.

"Social isolation and loneliness - the sad thing is in rural communities, people don't always like to talk about that and acknowledge that," he said.

Nine of the friends, including Mervyn and Ruth, found themselves singing in the choir as part of the King's Coronation concert .

They met the Duke and Duchess of Edinburgh, and Mervyn also met one of his heroes - Welsh bass-baritone Bryn Terfel, whose father was a sheep farmer.

"We were running around with these Farmers' Choir vests, and he spotted us and he stopped and talked to us," he said.

"I'm a teacher - teaching can be stressful and farmers have their stresses on the farm, and you can see it on their faces.

"They go into their practice,...
body.zh: 当牛结核病导致整个牛群死亡时，奶农默文·凯尔索 (Mervyn Kelso) 在空荡荡的田野和挤奶场的寂静中与悲伤作斗争。 对于一个一生务农的人来说，这是一段痛苦的时光，看着邻居照顾牛也很难过。 他的姐姐建议他加入农民合唱团，结果证明他是一名“伟大的举重运动员”。 四年过去了，默文为国王演唱，会见了音乐界的皇室成员，他的合唱团即将获得国家奖项。 Mervyn 的第一批奶牛于 2021 年 11 月丢失。与此同时，一位在安特里姆郡农场生活了三代的朋友也去世了。 住在波特格莱诺附近的默文和他的妻子露丝依靠他们的信仰来“继续前进”。 默文会在教堂唱歌，因此当农民合唱团那年秋天在附近的巴利米纳重新开始时，他决定尝试一下。 他说，这是有益且不同的——缓解了日常农业的严峻挑战。 “农业是一项非常孤独的工作，甚至比上一代人更加孤独，因为劳动力很难获得，”他说。 “它会让你感到沮丧，这就是为什么参加合唱团或农业以外的任何社交活动对任何人都有好处。” “这对我们俩来说都是一段艰难的时光，合唱团绝对是一位伟大的举重运动员，”她说。 “能有一些东西来鼓舞我们真是太好了，因为你在农场并不忙——嗯，你做了一些额外的零工，但这并不像平常那​​样忙碌。” 她说她结识了“一些可爱的朋友”，他们可以在合唱团排练、音乐会和聚会上见面。 “有时，当你不只是坐在合唱团成员旁边唱歌时，你会看到他们的不同侧面，这在社交方面真的很好，”她补充道。 他在一个奶牛场长大，记得父亲在收获季节谈论人们，互相帮助，然后分享“一些疯狂和玩笑”。 他说，随着农业变得更加自动化，合唱团帮助填补了农村生活中出现的社会差距。 “社会孤立和孤独——可悲的是在农村社区，人们并不总是喜欢谈论并承认这一点，”他说。 包括默文和露丝在内的九位朋友发现自己在合唱团中唱歌，作为国王加冕音乐会的一部分。 他们遇到了爱丁堡公爵和公爵夫人，默文还遇到了他的英雄之一——威尔士男中音布林·特菲尔，他的父亲是一位牧羊人。 “我们穿着这些农民合唱团的背心跑来跑去，他发现了我们，然后停下来和我们说话，”他说。 “我是一名老师——教学压力很大，农民在农场也有压力，你可以从他们的脸上看到。 “他们开始练习，......

reflection.en: The silence of Mervyn Kelso's fields after losing his herd to bovine TB speaks of deep loss and despair. Yet, when he joined the Farmers' Choir, he found his strength renewed, much like the prophet's promise that those who wait for Yahweh will soar on wings like eagles. His story shows that even in the face of devastating loss, new life and purpose can be...
reflection.zh: Mervyn Kelso 在因牛结核病失去牛群后，田野的寂静诉说着深切的失落和绝望。然而，当他加入农民合唱团时，他找到了力量的更新，这与先知应许那些等候雅伟的人必如鹰展翅上腾的应许相似。他的故事表明，即使面对毁灭性的损失，也能通过意想不到的途径找到新的生命和目标。

verse.textEn: Those who hope in Yahweh will renew their strength. They will soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary.
verse.textZh: 但那等候雅伟的，必从新得力。他们必如鹰展翅上腾。

title.en: Take good care of your tailbone. I didn’t – and my derriere has never been the same since | Adrian Chiles
title.zh: 好好照顾你的尾骨。我没有——我的臀部从此再也不同了 | 阿德里安·奇尔斯

summary.en: The author reflects on persistent tailbone pain from an extreme cycling challenge nearly two decades ago, linking it to the common ailments of middle and approaching old age. He notes his GP's dismissive 'welcome to middle age' and his own increasing reliance on this phrase to explain his various aches and pains,...
summary.zh: 作者回顾了近二十年前一次极限自行车挑战留下的持续性尾骨疼痛，并将其与中老年常见的各种病痛联系起来。他提到医生曾以“欢迎来到中年”来回应他关于健康问题的询问，而如今他自己也常常用这句话来解释自己身体的各种不适，尤其是肩膀的剧痛，使得一些简单的日常动作都需要仔细规划。

body.en: My coccyx still hurts from an extreme cycling challenge almost two decades ago. Is there anything it’s good for? ‘Welcome to middle age.” This is what my GP said to me 10 years ago when I asked her why I needed this pill or that. Being then just shy of 50, that hit home. Now being just shy of 60, I mutter those words to myself at least once a day. There’s a long list of aches, pains and assorted maladies about which to mutter. High up on that list are my shoulders. Bloody agony, both of them. Picking something off a high shelf or fishing for something on the back seat of the car have had to become planned events to be undertaken only if absolutely necessary. I interviewed Prof Alice Roberts this week. A writer, broadcaster, academic, anatomist, archaeologist and sometime medical doctor, she knows her bones, and no mistake. I noted with interest that her PhD thesis was titled “Rotator cuff disease in humans and apes: a palaeopathological and evolutionary perspective on shoulder pathology”. I’ve rarely felt so connected with my ancestors, so human, and indeed so ape-like. In an instant my shoulder pain became easier to bear, as I felt at one with a caveman wincing as he reached up to apply the finishing touches to some wall art. Continue reading...
body.zh: 我的尾骨仍然因二十年前的一次极限自行车挑战而疼痛。它有什么好处吗？ “欢迎来到中年。”这是 10 年前，当我问我的全科医生为什么需要这种药或那种药时，她对我说的。当时还不到 50 岁，这一点击中了要害。现在我还不到60岁，我每天至少对自己念叨一次这些话。有一长串的疼痛和各种疾病值得抱怨。这份名单上最靠前的是我的肩膀。血淋淋的痛苦，他们俩。从高架上挑选东西或在汽车后座上钓鱼必须成为计划中的活动，只有在绝对必要时才进行。本周我采访了爱丽丝·罗伯茨教授。作为一名作家、广播员、学者、解剖学家、考古学家，有时还兼任医生，她了解自己的骨头，而且没有任何错误。我感兴趣地注意到她的博士论文标题为“人类和猿的肩袖疾病：肩部病理学的古病理学和进化视角”。我很少感到与我的祖先如此紧密相连，如此人性化，而且确实如此像猿猴。刹那间，我的肩膀疼痛变得更容易忍受了，就像我感觉到一个穴居人在伸手对一些壁画进行最后的润色时皱起眉头。继续阅读...

reflection.en: As we navigate the inevitable physical changes that come with age, the author's experience with persistent pain serves as a poignant reminder of our mortality. The Psalmist's prayer to 'number our days' encourages us to approach life with wisdom, appreciating each season and seeking understanding even amidst discomfort and decline. May we find grace to care...
reflection.zh: 随着年龄的增长，我们不可避免地会经历身体的变化，作者的经历提醒我们生命的有限性。诗篇作者祈求“数算我们的日子”，鼓励我们以智慧度日，珍惜每个季节，并在困苦和衰老中寻求理解。愿我们能蒙恩惠，好好照顾自己的身体，认识到它们是暂时的器皿，并以日渐增长的智慧与平安之心来面对衰老。

verse.textEn: Teach us to number our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.
verse.textZh: 求你指教我们怎样数算自己的日子，好叫我们得着智慧的心。

title.en: ‘Very messy eaters’: scientists solve the mystery of when black holes ‘burp’
title.zh: “非常挑食”：科学家解开黑洞“打嗝”之谜

summary.en: Astronomical bodies fire off powerful jets in two distinct phases in their feeding cycle, researchers discover. Scientists have solved the mystery of when black holes “burp” – when the astronomical bodies launch jets after feeding on stars, blasting material enormous distances in space. Black holes are objects so...
summary.zh: 天体在进食周期中分两个不同阶段喷射出强大的喷流，研究人员发现。科学家们解开了黑洞“打嗝”之谜——即天体在吞噬恒星后喷射出喷流，将物质以巨大的能量喷射到太空中。黑洞是密度极高的天体，其引力强大到一定程度后，连光和物质都无法逃逸。这个不归点被称为事件视界——即逃逸需要速度超过光速的点。

body.en: The astronomical bodies fire off powerful jets in two distinct phases in their feeding cycle, researchers discover Scientists have solved the mystery of when black holes “burp” – when the astronomical bodies launch jets after feeding on stars, blasting material enormous distances in space. Black holes are objects so densely compact that beyond a certain point their gravity is too strong for light and matter to escape. This boundary of no return is known as the event horizon – the point at which escaping would require something to travel faster than the speed of light. Continue reading...
body.zh: 研究人员发现，这些天体在其进食周期的两个不同阶段发射出强大的喷射流，科学家们已经解决了黑洞何时“打嗝”的谜团——当天体在吞噬恒星后发射喷射流，将物质在太空中喷射出很远的距离。黑洞是一种非常致密的物体，超过某一点，它们的引力就太强，光和物质都无法逃脱。这个不归路的边界被称为事件视界——在这个点上，物体的运动速度必须超过光速。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The universe is full of wonders, from the smallest organism to the grandest celestial bodies. Job 12:7 reminds us that creation itself is a teacher, offering profound insights into Yahweh's wisdom. By observing the complex and sometimes violent processes of black holes, scientists gain a deeper understanding of the cosmos, reflecting the intricate design of...
reflection.zh: 宇宙充满了奇迹，从最小的生物到最宏伟的天体。约伯记12:7提醒我们，创造本身就是一位老师，它提供了关于雅伟智慧的深刻见解。通过观察黑洞复杂甚至有时是剧烈的过程，科学家们对宇宙有了更深入的了解，这反映了我们造物主的精妙设计。

verse.textEn: But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you; or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you.
verse.textZh: 你且问走兽，走兽必指教你；又问空中的飞鸟，飞鸟必告诉你。或与地说话，地必指教你；海中的鱼也必向你说明。

title.en: New mesothelioma drug turns cancer’s own defenses against it
title.zh: 新型间皮瘤药物利用癌细胞自身防御机制

summary.en: Scientists are investigating a novel approach to treating mesothelioma, a difficult-to-treat cancer linked to asbestos exposure. An experimental drug targets and disables PRX3, an antioxidant defense that enables tumors to withstand severe oxidative stress. Early clinical trials show promising results, with 67% of...
summary.zh: 科学家正在研究一种治疗间皮瘤的新方法，这是一种与石棉暴露有关的难以治疗的癌症。一种实验性药物通过靶向并禁用PRX3来起作用，PRX3是一种抗氧化防御机制，使肿瘤能够承受严重的氧化应激。早期临床试验显示出有希望的结果，67%的患者的疾病进展得到控制，并且生存率令人鼓舞，这激发了将其应用于其他癌症的希望。

body.en: Scientists are testing a counterintuitive way to fight mesothelioma, an aggressive asbestos-linked cancer with few effective treatments. A new experimental mesothelioma drug kills cancer cells by disabling PRX3, an antioxidant defense that tumors use to survive intense oxidative stress. In an early clinical trial, it controlled disease progression in 67% of patients and produced encouraging survival results, raising hopes that the strategy could eventually be used against other cancers.
body.zh: 科学家们正在测试一种违反直觉的方法来对抗间皮瘤，这是一种与石棉相关的侵袭性癌症，几乎没有有效的治疗方法。一种新的实验性间皮瘤药物通过禁用 PRX3 来杀死癌细胞，PRX3 是一种抗氧化防御系统，肿瘤用来生存强烈的氧化应激。在一项早期临床试验中，它控制了 67% 患者的疾病进展，并产生了令人鼓舞的生存结果，这让人们希望该策略最终可以用于治疗其他癌症。

reflection.en: The intricate workings of creation often hold the keys to overcoming life's challenges. This new drug's strategy, disabling a tumor's own survival mechanism, mirrors how we might learn to disarm the destructive patterns within ourselves by understanding their inner workings. May we continue to seek wisdom from the natural world, and apply it with compassion.
reflection.zh: 创造的复杂运作往往是克服生活挑战的关键。这种新药的策略是禁用肿瘤自身的生存机制，这与我们通过理解自身破坏性模式的内在运作来学习解除它们的方式相似。愿我们继续从自然界寻求智慧，并以同情心加以应用。

verse.textEn: But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you; or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you.
verse.textZh: 你且问走兽，走兽必指教你；又问空中的飞鸟，飞鸟必告诉你。或与地说话，地必指教你；海中的鱼也必向你说明。

title.en: Rare tree offspring given lifeline at Scottish botanic garden
title.zh: 苏格兰植物园为稀有树木后代提供生命线

summary.en: Logan Botanic Garden is assisting in the preservation of a tree species indigenous to Robinson Crusoe Island in the South Pacific. Conservationists are intensifying efforts to prevent the species from becoming extinct by establishing a new home for two seedlings from the last known wild dendroseris neriifolia tree,...
summary.zh: 洛根植物园正在协助保护一种原产于南太平洋鲁滨逊漂流者岛的树木。保护主义者正通过为世界上仅存的一棵野生 dendroseris neriifolia 树的两个幼苗建立新家，来加紧努力防止该物种灭绝，这棵树目前仅作为单一植株悬挂在悬崖上。

body.en:
The offspring of one of the world's rarest trees has been given a new home in south-west Scotland as conservationists step up efforts to save the species from extinction.

Two seedlings from the last known wild dendroseris neriifolia tree have arrived at Logan Botanic Garden in Dumfries and Galloway after an international rescue effort involving experts in Chile and the UK.

The species, native to Robinson Crusoe Island in the South Pacific, has been pushed to the brink by habitat loss, invasive species and repeated wildfires.

Conservationists hope the move will provide a vital safeguard for the future of a plant that now survives in the wild as a single tree clinging to a cliff face.

The dendroseris neriifolia, a rare tree daisy found only on Chile's Robinson Crusoe Island, has suffered a dramatic decline over recent decades.

By 1980, only eight wild specimens remained, and although reintroduction projects were launched in the early 2000s, the breakdown of protection measures in 2017 left the species vulnerable once again to invasive plants and grazing animals.

Today, the last surviving wild tree is supported by ropes on a steep volcanic outcrop to prevent it from falling.

In May this year, 29 seeds were collected from the lone tree and sent to the Millennium Seed Bank at Kew Wakehurst.

Eight seedlings successfully germinated, with two now transferred to Logan Botanic Garden, where the climate is considered particularly suitable for rare Chilean plants. The remaining seedlings will stay at Kew.

Richard Baines, curator at Logan, described the arrival as a significant moment and said the garden could play an important role in learning more about the species and helping secure its future.

"Experience shows that plant species from the Juan Fernández Islands do well at Logan," he said.

"Creating a safe place for these seedlings, getting to know them, and learning more about their adaption to different environments, gives us the chance to contribute so much more."

Scientists involved in the project said the international collaboration offered a rare opportunity to prevent the extinction of a unique plant lineage and preserve part of the natural heritage of the Juan Fernández archipelago.

Diego Penneckamp, a scientist at Jardín Botánico VerdeNativo, said saving the species was a "race against time".

"This international collaboration to support the last remaining individual could prevent the extinction of a species that represents a unique lineage with its own natural history," he said.
body.zh: 随着自然资源保护主义者加紧努力拯救该物种免遭灭绝，世界上最稀有的树木之一的后代在苏格兰西南部找到了新家。 经过智利和英国专家参与的国际救援努力，最后一棵已知的野生树突树的两棵幼苗已抵达邓弗里斯和加洛韦的洛根植物园。 该物种原产于南太平洋的鲁宾逊克鲁索岛，由于栖息地丧失、入侵物种和反复发生的野火，已被推向边缘。 环保主义者希望此举能为这种植物的未来提供重要的保障，这种植物目前在野外以单棵树的形式生存在悬崖表面。 树突花是一种仅在智利鲁宾逊克鲁索岛上发现的稀有雏菊，近几十年来其数量急剧减少。 到 1980 年，只剩下 8 个野生标本，尽管在 2000 年代初启动了重新引入项目，但 2017 年保护措施的崩溃使该物种再次容易受到入侵植物和食草动物的侵害。 如今，最后一棵幸存的野生树被绳索支撑在陡峭的火山露头上，以防止其倒下。 今年 5 月，人们从这棵孤树上收集了 29 粒种子，并送往位于 Kew Wakehurst 的千年种子库。 八棵幼苗成功发芽，其中两棵现已转移到洛根植物园，那里的气候被认为特别适合稀有的智利植物。剩下的幼苗将留在邱园。 洛根博物馆馆长理查德·贝恩斯 (Richard Baines) 将此次到来描述为一个重要时刻，并表示该花园可以在更多地了解该物种并帮助确保其未来方面发挥重要作用。 “经验表明，来自胡安·费尔南德斯群岛的植物物种在洛根生长得很好，”他说。 “为这些幼苗创造一个安全的地方，了解它们，并更多地了解它们对不同环境的适应，使我们有机会做出更多贡献。” 参与该项目的科学家表示，国际合作提供了一个难得的机会，可以防止独特的植物谱系灭绝，并保护胡安·费尔南德斯群岛的部分自然遗产。 Jardín Botánico VerdeNativo 的科学家迭戈·彭内坎普 (Diego Penneckamp) 表示，拯救该物种是“与时间赛跑”。 他说：“这种支持最后一个个体的国际合作可以防止一个代表着具有自己的自然历史的独特谱系的物种的灭绝。”

reflection.en: In the face of extinction, conservationists have intervened to protect the rare dendroseris neriifolia tree, giving its young a chance to thrive. This act of stewardship mirrors the biblical mandate to care for the earth and its inhabitants, recognizing the intrinsic value of every living thing.
reflection.zh: 面对灭绝的威胁，保护主义者介入保护稀有的 dendroseris neriifolia 树，让它们的后代有机会茁壮成长。这种管理行为呼应了圣经中照顾大地及其居民的使命，认识到每一种生物的内在价值。

verse.textEn: Yahweh God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden to work it and take care of it.
verse.textZh: 雅伟神将那人安置在伊甸园，使他修理看守。

title.en: NASA’s New Horizons spots signs of liquid nitrogen flowing on Pluto
title.zh: 新视野号探测器发现冥王星上有液氮流动的迹象

summary.en: Scientists have found the first evidence that liquid may have flowed across Pluto’s surface in the recent past. Dark features on the enormous Sputnik Planitia glacier appear consistent with liquid nitrogen rising through cracks from deep beneath the ice. Computer models show that nitrogen could melt at the glacier’s...
summary.zh: 科学家们首次发现了液态物质可能在近期流过冥王星表面的证据。巨大的斯普特尼克平原冰川上的黑暗特征似乎与液氮从冰层深处通过裂缝上升的现象一致。计算机模型显示，氮气可以在冰川底部融化，并通过细小的管道向上流动。这一发现表明，冥王星的地质活动可能比其冰冻的外观所显示的要活跃得多。

body.en: Scientists have found the first evidence that liquid may have flowed across Pluto’s surface in the recent past. Dark features on the enormous Sputnik Planitia glacier appear consistent with liquid nitrogen rising through cracks from deep beneath the ice. Computer models show that nitrogen could melt at the glacier’s base and travel upward like fluid through small conduits. The finding reveals that Pluto may be much more geologically active than its frozen appearance suggests.
body.zh: 科学家们发现了第一个证据，表明液体在不久前可能流过冥王星表面。巨大的斯普特尼克平原冰川上的黑色特征似乎与从冰层深处的裂缝中升起的液氮一致。计算机模型显示，氮气可以在冰川底部融化，并像液体一样通过小管道向上流动。这一发现表明，冥王星的地质活动可能比其冰冻外观所暗示的要活跃得多。

reflection.en: The vastness of the cosmos and the intricate workings of even the most distant celestial bodies continue to reveal the boundless wisdom of our Creator. The discovery of geological activity on Pluto, a world once thought to be inert, reminds us that Yahweh's creation is far more dynamic and wondrous than we can fully comprehend. It invites awe and humility...
reflection.zh: 宇宙的浩瀚以及即使是最遥远天体的复杂运作，不断揭示着我们造物主的无限智慧。在曾经被认为是一片死寂的冥王星上发现地质活动的迹象，提醒我们雅伟的创造比我们所能完全理解的要活跃和奇妙得多。当我们探索祂所造的宇宙时，这邀请我们怀着敬畏和谦卑之心。

verse.textEn: How many are your works, Yahweh! In wisdom you made them all; the earth is full of your creatures.
verse.textZh: 雅伟啊，你所造的何其多！都是你用智慧造成的；遍地满了你的丰富。

title.en: The week that changed maths for ever – podcast
title.zh: 改变数学的‘一周’——播客

summary.en: In early September, OpenAI announced it had solved a major mathematics problem that has stumped humans for nearly a century. The news left mathematicians reeling, and many expressed concern over what will be left for humans as AI becomes ever more adept at unravelling complex problems. Now 25 recipients of the Fields...
summary.zh: 九月初，OpenAI宣布已解决一个困扰人类近百年的重大数学难题。这一消息令数学界震惊，许多人担心随着人工智能在解开复杂问题方面越来越得心应手，人类将何去何从。如今，25位菲尔兹奖（常被称为数学界的诺贝尔奖）得主联名发表公开信，表达了对人工智能公司与其领域之间“严重脱节”的担忧。为了解人工智能将如何颠覆数学——以及数学家...

body.en: In early September, OpenAI announced it had solved a major mathematics problem that has stumped humans for nearly a century. The news left mathematicians reeling, and many expressed concern over what will be left for humans as AI becomes ever more adept at unravelling complex problems. Now 25 recipients of the Fields medal – often called the Nobel prize for maths – have signed an open letter expressing their fears of a ‘severe misalignment’ between AI companies and their field. To find out how AI is likely to upend maths – and how mathematicians might respond – Ian Sample speaks to Colva Roney-Dougal, professor of pure mathematics at the University of St Andrews ‘Immature playground boasting’: mathematicians uneasy at OpenAI’s latest scalp Support the Guardian: theguardian.com/sciencepod Continue reading...
body.zh: 9月初，OpenAI宣布解决了困扰人类近一个世纪的重大数学问题。这一消息让数学家感到震惊，许多人对随着人工智能变得越来越擅长解决复杂问题而给人类留下的东西表示担忧。现在，菲尔兹奖（通常被称为数学诺贝尔奖）的 25 名获得者签署了一封公开信，表达了他们对人工智能公司与其领域之间“严重脱节”的担忧。为了了解人工智能可能如何颠覆数学，以及数学家会如何应对，Ian Sample 与圣安德鲁斯大学纯数学教授 Colva Roney-Dougal 进行了对话“不成熟的操场吹嘘”：数学家对 OpenAI 的最新头皮感到不安 支持卫报：theguardian.com/sciencepod 继续阅读...

reflection.en: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence, exemplified by OpenAI solving a century-old math problem, echoes the ancient prophecy that 'knowledge shall increase' in the latter days. This technological leap, while astounding, also raises profound questions about humanity's role and purpose in an increasingly intelligent world. As we witness these...
reflection.zh: 人工智能的飞速发展，例如OpenAI解决了百年数学难题，呼应了古老的预言——在末世“知识必增长”。这项技术飞跃虽然令人惊叹，但也引发了关于人类在日益智能化的世界中的角色和目的的深刻问题。当我们见证这些发展时，我们被呼召寻求智慧和分辨力，确保我们对知识的追求能造福所有人。

verse.textEn: But you, Daniel, roll up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.
verse.textZh: 但以理啊，你要隐藏这话，封闭这书，直到末时。必有多人来往奔跑，知识就必增长。

title.en: Climate crisis probably weakened glacier that caused devastating Nepal-Tibet floods, first study finds
title.zh: 气候危机可能削弱了导致尼泊尔-西藏毁灭性洪水的冰川，首次研究发现

summary.en: Scientists say global heating was a destabilising factor in the collapse of a 200,000 sq metre glacier in August. Climate breakdown probably weakened the glacier that collapsed, causing catastrophic floods and killing over a thousand people in Nepal and Tibet last month, the first scientific study of the disaster has...
summary.zh: 科学家表示，全球变暖是今年八月一个面积达20万平方米的冰川崩塌的破坏因素。首次对此次灾难进行的科学研究发现，气候变化可能削弱了导致冰川崩塌的因素，造成了灾难性的洪水，并导致上个月尼泊尔和西藏一千多人丧生。研究人员在冰川崩塌前发现了异常的温暖条件，崩塌导致1.1亿立方米的冰雪倾泻到山谷中，引发了前所未有的大规模洪水。

body.en: Scientists say global heating was a destabilising factor in collapse of 200,000 sq metre glacier in August Climate breakdown probably weakened the glacier that collapsed causing catastrophic floods and killing over a thousand people in Nepal and Tibet last month, the first scientific study of the disaster has found. Researchers identified unusually warm conditions before the glacier’s collapse , which sent an avalanche of 110m cubic metres (3.885bn cu ft) of snow and ice into the valley below. This triggered flash floods on an almost unprecedented scale, hitting communities downstream without warning. Continue reading...
body.zh: 科学家表示，全球变暖是导致 8 月份 20 万平方米冰川崩塌的不稳定因素。第一项针对这场灾难的科学研究发现，气候崩溃可能削弱了上个月崩塌的冰川，导致尼泊尔和西藏发生灾难性洪水，造成千余人死亡。研究人员在冰川崩塌之前发现了异常温暖的气候，导致 1.1 亿立方米（38.85 亿立方英尺）的雪和冰雪崩进入下面的山谷。这引发了几乎前所未有的规模的山洪，毫无预警地袭击了下游社区。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The earth itself groans under the weight of human impact, as this study suggests climate breakdown destabilized a glacier, leading to devastating floods. This echoes the Apostle Paul's observation that all of creation waits with eager longing for its redemption. May we be mindful of our stewardship and seek ways to heal the world entrusted to us.
reflection.zh: 大地本身也在承受人类活动带来的重负而叹息，正如这项研究表明气候崩溃破坏了冰川的稳定性，导致了毁灭性的洪水。这呼应了使徒保罗所言，万物都在等候神的儿女显明出来，一同得着释放。愿我们谨记所领受的管家之责，并寻求方法医治这托付给我们的世界。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Top Trump military adviser says US must prepare to fight around moon
title.zh: 特朗普军事顾问称美军须准备绕月球作战

summary.en: General Dan Caine, a top military adviser to Donald Trump, stated that US troops must prepare for combat not only in Earth's orbit but also around the moon. These comments follow the US's recent revelation that it has deployed weapons in space, signaling a new frontier in warfare.
summary.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统的首席军事顾问丹·凯恩将军表示，美军不仅要在地球轨道上，还必须准备在月球周围作战。此番言论是在美国首次披露已在太空部署武器之后发表的，预示着战争的新领域。

body.en: Gen Dan Caine’s comments at Washington summit come after US revealed it has deployed weapons in space US troops need to prepare for combat not only in Earth’s orbit but around the moon, Donald Trump’s top military adviser said on Wednesday, looking ahead to a new frontier in warfare after the US revealed for the first time that it has deployed weapons in space. Gen Dan Caine, chairman of the joint chiefs of staff, told service members and industry figures at the Air, Space and Cyber Conference outside Washington that the US military should adapt now so it “is prepared to fight, endure and win … from the seabed to cislunar space”. Continue reading...
body.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普的高级军事顾问周三表示，在美国透露已在太空部署武器后，丹·凯恩将军在华盛顿峰会上发表上述言论，美国军队不仅需要为地球轨道上的战斗做好准备，还需要为绕月作战做好准备，在美国首次透露已在太空部署武器后，展望了战争的新领域。参谋长联席会议主席丹·凯恩将军在华盛顿郊外举行的航空、航天和网络会议上对军人和业界人士表示，美国军方现在应该做出调整，以便“做好战斗、忍受和胜利的准备……从海底到地月空间”。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The prospect of warfare extending to the moon and beyond raises profound questions about humanity's trajectory. Isaiah's vision of a future where nations 'beat their swords into plowshares' offers a stark contrast to this escalating militarization. May we seek paths of peace and disarmament, turning our ingenuity towards creation and cooperation rather than...
reflection.zh: 战争可能延伸至月球及更远之处的前景，引发了关于人类发展轨迹的深刻问题。以赛亚先知预言的“将刀打成犁头”的未来景象，与这种不断升级的军事化形成了鲜明对比。愿我们寻求和平与裁军的道路，将我们的智慧用于创造与合作，而非冲突。

verse.textEn: They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks.
verse.textZh: 他们要将刀打成犁头，把枪打成镰刀。

title.en: Women with same health conditions as men ‘less likely to be offered active treatment’
title.zh: 患有与男性相同疾病的女性“不太可能接受积极治疗”

summary.en: A global analysis reveals that men with heart, kidney, or liver conditions are more likely to receive interventions compared to women. The research indicates that for several health issues, including cardiovascular diseases, kidney disease, and Parkinson's, women receive less treatment than men, demonstrating...
summary.zh: 一项全球分析显示，患有心脏、肾脏或肝脏疾病的男性比女性更有可能接受治疗。研究表明，对于包括心血管疾病、肾脏疾病和帕金森病在内的几种健康问题，女性接受的治疗少于男性，这表明医疗保健方面存在显著的不平等。

body.en: Men with heart, kidney or liver conditions more likely to be offered intervention compared with women, global analysis finds Women with the same medical condition as men are less likely to be offered treatment such as surgery, a stent or a strong painkiller, research has found. A review of global research found that for several health problems, including cardiovascular conditions, kidney disease and Parkinson’s, women were less likely to receive the same treatment as men, revealing the extent to which women have significantly unequal care. Continue reading...
body.zh: 研究发现，与女性相比，患有心脏、肾脏或肝脏疾病的男性更有可能接受干预，研究发现，与男性健康状况相同的女性接受手术、支架或强效止痛药等治疗的可能性较小。一项对全球研究的回顾发现，对于包括心血管疾病、肾脏疾病和帕金森氏症在内的多种健康问题，女性接受与男性相同治疗的可能性较小，这揭示了女性所享受的护理存在明显不平等的程度。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This research points to a concerning disparity where women receive less medical intervention than men for the same conditions. It calls to mind the call to speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, ensuring their needs are met and their voices are heard in all aspects of life, including healthcare. May we advocate for fairness and equal treatment,...
reflection.zh: 这项研究揭示了一个令人担忧的差距，即女性在患有相同疾病的情况下接受的医疗干预比男性少。这让人想起为那些不能为自己说话的人发声的呼召，确保他们在生活的各个方面，包括医疗保健中，都能得到满足其需求并听到他们的声音。 愿我们倡导公平和平等的待遇，确保所有个体，无论性别，都能获得他们应得的关怀。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Part-human part-mouse brain developed in science breakthrough
title.zh: 科学突破：部分人脑部分鼠脑在实验中被开发出来

summary.en: Researchers at Stanford University have genetically modified mice to accept and integrate human brain cells, a breakthrough that could lead to new treatments for human-specific neurological and psychiatric diseases.
summary.zh: 斯坦福大学的研究人员通过基因改造小鼠，使其能够接受并整合人类脑细胞，这项突破有望为仅在人类身上发生的神经和精神疾病带来新的治疗方法。

body.en:
Neuroscientists in the US have successfully adapted mice to have functioning human cells inside their own brains.

The researchers hope that potential treatments for psychiatric and neurodevelopmental diseases that only occur in humans could now be tested on the laboratory rodents.

While mice with brains that are partly human might sound like a Kafkaesque experiment, the scientists said these are not "mice that think like humans".

The animals are genetically engineered - and surgically altered - so that some of their brain tissue is human.

The scientists said their work, published in the journal Nature , external , was carried out with independent ethical scrutiny.

The aim of this ethically complicated breakthrough was to better understand the biology of brain disorders for which there are currently no effective treatments.

Some conditions cannot be studied in a mouse, simply because rodents do not develop some of the brain disorders that we do.

As lead researcher Prof Sergiu Pașca from Stanford University explained in a press conference, psychiatry has "one of the lowest success rates for clinical trials".

"Even drugs that actually make it to clinical trial - that seem to be working really well in animal models - fail dramatically in clinic," he said in a press conference. "That tells us we're missing a lot of information about human biology and capturing that will be essential."

The Stanford researchers said that, for some complex conditions, including epilepsy, autism and cerebral palsy, it has the potential to be "transformative".

Pașca said: "Here we have a new model that allows us to actually capture aspects of human brain function in a way that has not been possible before."

The human brain is made up of billions of cells, interconnected in millions of circuits, making it difficult to understand its development and what exactly is happening – at the cellular level - when things go wrong.

While this research is not the first time human neurons have been implanted in laboratory rodents , external , these scientists took that approach to a new level.

First, they genetically-engineered mice to develop almost none of their own cerebral cortex – that is the outer layer of the brain sometimes referred to as "grey matter". It handles higher-level thinking, memory and senses.

The researchers then used skin cells taken from humans and "reprogrammed" them, so they grew into pieces of brain-like tissue.

These are structures called organoids – they are not whole brains grown in dishes, more collections of connected, living cells.

When these organoids were implanted into the mouse brain the cells divided and organised themselves into the animal's existing brain circuitry, connecting with the rest of the mouse's brain and spinal cord.

The...
body.zh: 美国的神经科学家已经成功地让老鼠在自己的大脑中拥有了功能正常的人类细胞。 研究人员希望，针对仅发生在人类身上的精神和神经发育疾病的潜在治疗方法现在可以在实验室啮齿动物身上进行测试。 虽然具有部分人类大脑的老鼠听起来像是卡夫卡式的实验，但科学家们表示，这些老鼠并不是“像人类一样思考的老鼠”。 这些动物经过基因工程改造，并通过手术改变，因此它们的一些脑组织是人类的。 科学家们表示，他们发表在《自然》杂志上的研究成果是经过独立的伦理审查的。 这一伦理上复杂的突破的目的是更好地了解目前尚无有效治疗方法的脑部疾病的生物学原理。 有些病症无法在小鼠身上进行研究，因为啮齿类动物不会出现我们所患的某些大脑疾病。 正如斯坦福大学首席研究员 Sergiu Paşca 教授在新闻发布会上解释的那样，精神病学是“临床试验成功率最低的学科之一”。 他在新闻发布会上说：“即使是真正进入临床试验的药物——在动物模型中似乎效果很好——但在临床上却急剧失败。” “这告诉我们，我们错过了很多有关人类生物学的信息，捕捉这些信息至关重要。” 斯坦福大学的研究人员表示，对于一些复杂的疾病，包括癫痫、自闭症和脑瘫，它有可能具有“变革性”。 帕斯卡说：“我们有了一个新模型，它使我们能够以一种以前不可能的方式真正捕捉人类大脑功能的各个方面。” 人脑由数十亿个细胞组成，通过数百万个电路相互连接，因此很难理解其发育以及当出现问题时在细胞水平上到底发生了什么。 虽然这项研究并不是第一次将人类神经元植入实验室啮齿动物体内，但这些科学家将这种方法提升到了一个新的水平。 首先，他们对小鼠进行基因改造，使其几乎不发育出自己的大脑皮层——即大脑的外层，有时被称为“灰质”。它处理更高层次的思维、记忆和感官。 然后，研究人员使用取自人类的皮肤细胞并对它们进行“重新编程”，使它们长成类似大脑的组织碎片。 这些结构被称为类器官——它们不是在培养皿中生长的整个大脑，而是更多相连的活细胞的集合。 当这些类器官被植入小鼠大脑时，细胞分裂并组织成动物现有的大脑回路，与小鼠大脑和脊髓的其余部分连接。 这...

reflection.en: The creation of a hybrid human-mouse brain represents a significant leap in neuroscience. It reminds us that the intricate workings of the brain, whether in humans or mice, are part of Yahweh's marvelous creation. Through careful study and ethical consideration, science can uncover deeper insights into life itself, reflecting the wisdom inherent in the...
reflection.zh: 人鼠杂交大脑的创造是神经科学的重大飞跃。它提醒我们，无论是人类还是小鼠的大脑，其错综复杂的工作方式都是雅伟奇妙创造的一部分。通过严谨的研究和伦理考量，科学可以揭示生命本身的更深层见解，反映出自然界固有的智慧。

verse.textEn: But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you; or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you.
verse.textZh: 你且问走兽，走兽必指教你；又问空中的飞鸟，飞鸟必告诉你。或与地说话，地必指教你；海中的鱼也必向你说明。

The decision follows a ruling that fake videos, including one showing a Labour councillor making...

Continue reading...

reflection.en: The proliferation of AI-generated deepfakes presents a significant challenge to discerning truth online. As seen with the videos targeting a UK politician and a Muslim campaigner, these fabricated images can spread misinformation and harm reputations. The call for stronger safeguards underscores the need for integrity in our digital communications,...
reflection.zh: 人工智能生成的深度伪造内容的泛滥，给在线辨别真相带来了重大挑战。正如针对英国政界人士和穆斯林活动人士的视频所示，这些虚假图像会传播错误信息并损害声誉。呼吁加强安全措施，凸显了在数字交流中保持诚信的必要性，这呼应了圣经关于说实话、避免欺骗的告诫。

verse.textEn: Therefore each of you must put off falsehood and speak truthfully to your neighbor.
verse.textZh: 所以你们要弃绝谎言，各人与邻舍说实话。

title.en: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands
title.zh: 查尔斯国王警告人工智能落入不法之徒手中存在“生存危险”

summary.en: King Charles has convened a summit with AI leaders, including representatives from Nvidia, OpenAI, and Anthropic, to discuss the potential "existential dangers" of artificial intelligence falling into the wrong hands. This meeting occurs amidst growing industry concerns about the rapid advancement of AI and the need...
summary.zh: 查尔斯国王召集了一次人工智能领导人峰会，与会者包括来自英伟达、OpenAI和Anthropic的代表，以讨论人工智能落入不法之徒手中可能带来的“生存危险”。此次会议正值业界对人工智能的快速发展以及监管必要性日益担忧之际。

body.en:
King Charles has warned AI executives of the "existential dangers" posed by the technology falling into the wrong hands.

He made the comments at a summit he had convened at Dumfries House in Ayrshire to discuss how the tech can be used to benefit society.

Those gathered at the meeting also included Kanishka Narayan, the UK's AI Minister, the Pope's advisor, and participants from AI giants such as Nvidia, OpenAI and Anthropic.

It comes amid a series of recent warnings from people inside the industry about the rapidly evolving capabilities of advanced or "frontier" AI models and the regulation needed to keep them in check.

"Those who have created these technologies are now increasingly warning that AI risks developing darker capacities - perhaps even to take life," the King told the executives.

He said there seemed to be an "urgency" in "adequately considering the existential dangers of such technologies falling into the wrong hands, and being used in potentially catastrophic ways".

"The task before you is not merely to advance technology, but to ensure that it remains firmly in the service of humanity, community and the natural world," he told the group.

The summit has been called to consider whether a "shared set of principles" can be developed to "help guide the future application" of AI.

Jensen Huang, chief executive of Nvidia, was among top industry leaders attending.

Nvidia is a central player in AI infrastructure, supplying chips to leading AI model developers including OpenAI and Meta.

It is also the world's most valuable company, with a stock market value of around $5.15tn.

Huang told the room he believed safety was "paramount", adding that companies should hold back a product and "keep engineering" if it was not safe enough.

The Nvidia boss also highlighted the value of open models - systems which give users direct access to the software - as a way to "ensure that people and countries are not left behind".

He said these systems must also be protected so "researchers, universities, start-ups and countries" can develop applications "none of us would have imagined alone".

"Let us lead with responsible optimism, build AI safely and securely, open it to more people, expand our ambition and solve the problems that matter to the world," Huang added.

Meanwhile Sir Demis Hassabis, who co-founded the UK AI lab DeepMind - later acquired by Google - offered a more cautious view on the pace of development.

He said artificial general intelligence - systems it is believed could be as good as or better than humans at multiple tasks - was "probably only a few short years away" and could have an impact "ten times that of the Industrial Revolution".

But he advocated for "a sensible middle way", saying humanity could address risks if...
body.zh: 查尔斯国王警告人工智能高管，该技术落入坏人之手将带来“生存危险”。 他在艾尔郡邓弗里斯大厦召开的峰会上发表了上述言论，讨论如何利用这项技术造福社会。 出席会议的还包括英国人工智能大臣、教皇顾问卡尼什卡·纳拉扬（Kanishka Narayan），以及来自 Nvidia、OpenAI 和 Anthropic 等人工智能巨头的与会者。 与此同时，业内人士最近就先进或“前沿”人工智能模型快速发展的能力以及控制它们所需的监管发出了一系列警告。 “那些创造这些技术的人现在越来越多地警告说，人工智能有可能发展出更黑暗的能力——甚至可能夺走生命，”国王告诉高管们。 他表示，“充分考虑此类技术落入坏人之手并以潜在灾难性方式使用所带来的生存危险”似乎是“紧迫的”。 “你们面前的任务不仅仅是推进技术，还要确保它坚定地为人类、社区和自然世界服务，”他告诉该组织。 此次峰会被要求考虑是否可以制定一套“共享原则”来“帮助指导人工智能的未来应用”。 Nvidia 首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 是出席会议的顶级行业领袖之一。 Nvidia 是人工智能基础设施领域的核心参与者，为 OpenAI 和 Meta 等领先的人工智能模型开发商提供芯片。 它也是世界上最有价值的公司，股票市值约为 5.15 兆美元。 黄告诉在场的人，他认为安全是“最重要的”，并补充说，如果产品不够安全，公司应该保留产品并“继续进行工程设计”。 这位英伟达老板还强调了开放模型（让用户直接访问软件的系统）的价值，作为“确保人民和国家不落后”的一种方式。 他表示，这些系统也必须受到保护，以便“研究人员、大学、初创企业和国家”能够开发“我们谁都无法单独想象的”应用程序。 黄补充道：“让我们以负责任的乐观态度引领，安全可靠地构建人工智能，向更多人开放，扩大我们的雄心，解决对世界至关重要的问题。” 与此同时，英国人工智能实验室 DeepMind（后来被谷歌收购）的联合创始人 Demis Hassabis 爵士对发展速度提出了更为谨慎的看法。 他表示，通用人工智能——人们相信在多项任务上可以与人类一样好甚至更好的系统——“可能只需要短短几年的时间”就会出现，并且可能产生“十倍于工业革命的影响”。 但他主张“明智的中间道路”，并表示人类可以应对风险，如果......

reflection.en: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence, as discussed at King Charles's summit, brings both immense potential and significant risks. The warning about AI falling into the wrong hands echoes the biblical understanding that increased knowledge and technological prowess can be a double-edged sword, requiring careful ethical consideration and wisdom.
reflection.zh: 查尔斯国王峰会上讨论的人工智能的快速发展，带来了巨大的潜力和重大的风险。关于人工智能落入不法之徒手中的警告，呼应了圣经中关于知识和技术能力增长可能是一把双刃剑的理解，这需要仔细的伦理考量和智慧。

verse.textEn: But you, Daniel, roll up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.
verse.textZh: 但以理啊，你要隐藏这话，封闭这书，直到末时。必有多人来往奔跑，知识就必增长。

Continue reading...

reflection.en: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence, as highlighted by OpenAI's disclosures, mirrors the biblical prophecy of knowledge increasing in the latter days. While this progress brings potential benefits, it also raises profound ethical questions and the need for careful stewardship of powerful new technologies. We are called to approach these...
reflection.zh: 正如 OpenAI 的披露所强调的，人工智能的快速发展与圣经中关于末世知识增长的预言相呼应。虽然这种进步带来了潜在的好处，但也引发了深刻的伦理问题，以及审慎管理强大新技术的必要性。我们被呼召以智慧和辨别力来应对这些发展，确保它们服务于人类，而不是削弱人类。

verse.textEn: But you, Daniel, roll up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.
verse.textZh: 但以理啊，你要隐藏这话，封闭这书，直到末时。必有多人来往奔跑，知识就必增长。

The government's consideration of a ban on smart glasses highlights the need to carefully evaluate how these tools impact our shared spaces and personal boundaries. reflection.zh: 新技术常常带来便利和创新的承诺，但正如这个故事所示，它们也带来了关于隐私和安全的复杂问题。政府考虑禁止智能眼镜，凸显了在这些工具普及之前，需要仔细评估它们如何影响我们的公共空间和个人界限。就像在火炉中试炼金属一样，新技术必须被审视其真正的价值和潜在的危害。

title.en: Why are there concerns AI could threaten humanity, and how real are they?
title.zh: 为什么担心人工智能会威胁人类，它们有多真实？

summary.en: Existential fears about AI have once again reared their head - here's what you need to know.
summary.zh: 关于人工智能的生存恐惧再次抬头——以下是您需要了解的信息。

body.en:
A slew of warnings about the potential dangers of AI have spurred calls for coordinated action to slow the technology's development.

Claims by current and former researchers that the tech will endanger humanity - with one suggesting there is a greater than 10% chance of it " killing all humans " - have raised alarm bells.

Major developers OpenAI and Anthropic are urging lawmakers to regulate AI, with Microsoft's AI boss the latest to say rules are needed to prevent a "silicon species" from eventually competing with humanity .

But some have dismissed the calls as an effort by big AI developers to cement their dominance over rivals.

Some AI researchers say there are worrying signs of systems developing in their capabilities and power too quickly.

Evan Hubinger, made headlines with his belief that there is a greater than 10% chance AI "could kill all humans" within the next decade.

He works in alignment, a field which aims to build human ethical ideas and principles into AI - essentially keeping it on track with what humans value.

While he said the risk from current systems was "low", his comments came as another researcher quit Anthropic and warned those developing the tech were losing their grip on it.

Jacob Coxon told the BBC he and other staff were "genuinely frightened" about the speed of advancements and what it could mean for humanity.

These concerns are the latest in a long line of fears about AI's potential to threaten humanity should it grow to match or surpass human abilities.

Such worries date back decades, with Alan Turing writing in the 1950s that should intelligent machines become possible, they could take control.

In the last few years, major AI companies have been racing to develop increasingly capable systems, both for profit and in pursuit of creating what they call super intelligence - theoretical tech which is smarter than humans.

Unlike the systems and tools many people use daily to complete tasks like writing emails or generating videos, super intelligent AI systems should be able to handle far more complex tasks.

OpenAI and Anthropic say they aim to advance such tech in a way which benefits humans and protect them from its existential risks.

But some critics believe machines can never truly match humans. They say AI firms exaggerate the tech's abilities to boost their prominence or profit.

AI researchers, experts and bosses worried about the technology's potential to endanger humanity have outlined unsettling scenarios.

Dario Amodei wrote in September , external it had advanced "drastically faster" than expected, including in its "ability to build the next generation of AI".

This is the concern that AI, after it has reached a certain point, could theoretically begin improving itself without human...
body.zh: 关于人工智能潜在危险的一系列警告促使人们呼吁采取协调行动以减缓该技术的发展。 现任和前任研究人员声称这项技术将危及人类——其中一位研究人员表示它“杀死所有人类”的可能性超过 10%——已经敲响了警钟。 主要开发商 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 正在敦促立法者监管人工智能，微软人工智能负责人最新表示，需要制定规则来防止“硅物种”最终与人类竞争。 但一些人驳斥了这些呼吁，认为这是大型人工智能开发商为巩固其对竞争对手的主导地位而做出的努力。 一些人工智能研究人员表示，有令人担忧的迹象表明系统的能力和能力发展得太快。 Evan Hubinger 因相信人工智能在未来十年内“杀死所有人类”的可能性超过 10% 而成为头条新闻。 他致力于将人类伦理思想和原则融入人工智能领域——本质上是让它与人类价值观保持一致。 虽然他表示当前系统的风险“很低”，但他发表此番言论之际，另一位研究人员退出了 Anthropic，并警告那些开发该技术的人正在失去对它的控制。 雅各布·考克森 (Jacob Coxon) 告诉英国广播公司 (BBC)，他和其他工作人员对进步的速度及其对人类意味着什么感到“真正感到害怕”。 这些担忧是人们对人工智能可能会威胁人类的一系列担忧中的最新一个，如果它发展到与人类能力相匹配或超越的话。 这种担忧可以追溯到几十年前，阿兰·图灵在 20 世纪 50 年代写道，如果智能机器成为可能，它们就可以掌控一切。 在过去的几年里，主要的人工智能公司一直在竞相开发功能越来越强大的系统，既是为了利润，也是为了创造他们所谓的超级智能——比人类更聪明的理论技术。 与许多人日常用来完成撰写电子邮件或生成视频等任务的系统和工具不同，超级智能人工智能系统应该能够处理更复杂的任务。 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 表示，他们的目标是以造福人类并保护他们免受生存风险的方式推进此类技术。 但一些批评家认为机器永远无法真正与人类相媲美。他们表示，人工智能公司夸大了该技术的能力，以提高其知名度或利润。 担心该技术可能危害人类的人工智能研究人员、专家和老板们概述了令人不安的场景。 达里奥·阿莫代 (Dario Amodei) 在 9 月份写道，从外部来看，它的进步比预期“快得多”，包括“构建下一代人工智能的能力”。 人们担心人工智能在达到一定程度后，理论上可以在没有人类的情况下开始自我改进......

reflection.en: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence brings with it profound questions about humanity's future and our place in the world. Warnings from researchers about AI potentially endangering humanity echo the ancient story of Babel, where human ambition to reach the heavens led to confusion. As we develop powerful new technologies, we are reminded to...
reflection.zh: 人工智能的飞速发展带来了关于人类未来和我们在世界中的地位的深刻问题。研究人员关于人工智能可能危及人类的警告，呼应了古代巴别塔的故事，当时人类 करण्याचा天に達する野心は混乱をもたらしました。私たちは強力な新技術を開発するにつれて、謙虚さと知恵をもって進み、創造物の究極の目的と影響を考慮することを思い出させられます。

verse.textEn: Yahweh said, 'If as one people speaking the same language they have begun to do this, then nothing they plan to do will be impossible for them.'
verse.textZh: 雅伟说：「看哪，他们成为一样的人民，都是一样的言语，如今既做起这事来，以后他们所要做的事就没有不成就的了。」

title.en: Big AI is trying to own the pathway to work. Universities shouldn’t play along | Ella Hafermalz
title.zh: 大型人工智能正试图掌控就业之路。大学不应随波逐流

summary.en: Universities must protect their educational standing to ensure students have an independent path to employment. AI companies like OpenAI are increasingly embedding themselves in the transition from education to work, potentially monopolizing it, which would be detrimental to students. Many students already use AI for...
summary.zh: 大学需要保护其教育地位，以确保学生拥有独立的就业途径。像OpenAI这样的人工智能公司正日益渗透到从教育到工作的过渡过程中，并可能将其完全垄断，这对学生来说将是灾难性的。许多学生已经将人工智能用于个人和学术问题，一些人甚至在没有人工智能的情况下怀疑自己的能力。

body.en: Universities need to protect their position in education so that students have an independent pathway to employment AI companies like OpenAI are insinuating themselves into the pathway from education to work. Soon they may claim it entirely, a disastrous result for students. We know that students are using AI at school and at university. In conversations with those I teach, I’m struck by the trust many place in it. They turn to ChatGPT and similar tools for personal problems as well as study help. Some even doubt their abilities without AI. Ella Hafermalz is an associate professor of work and technology at the Kin Center for Digital Innovation at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam Continue reading...
body.zh: 大学需要保护自己在教育中的地位，以便学生有独立的就业途径，像 OpenAI 这样的人工智能公司正在悄悄进入从教育到工作的途径。很快他们可能会完全声称拥有它，这对学生来说是灾难性的结果。我们知道学生在学校和大学都在使用人工智能。在与我所教的人的交谈中，我对其中许多地方的信任感到震惊。他们求助于 ChatGPT 和类似的工具来解决个人问题以及学习帮助。有些人甚至怀疑自己在没有人工智能的情况下的能力。 Ella Hafermalz 是阿姆斯特丹自由大学 Kin 数字创新中心的工作和技术副教授 继续阅读...

reflection.en: The article describes students placing immense trust in AI tools like ChatGPT, to the point of doubting their own abilities. This reliance raises questions about where true value and capability lie. Genesis 1:27 reminds us that humans are created in the image of God, possessing inherent dignity and worth independent of any technology.
reflection.zh: 文章描述了学生们对ChatGPT等人工智能工具寄予厚望，甚至怀疑自己的能力。这种依赖性引发了关于真正的价值和能力所在的问题。《创世记》1:27提醒我们，人是按照雅伟的形象所造，拥有内在的尊严和价值，这独立于任何技术。

verse.textEn: So God created mankind in his own image, in the image of God he created them; male and female he created them.
verse.textZh: 神就照着自己的形象造人，乃是照着他的形象造男造女。

title.en: Uncontrolled AI could lead to 'silicon species' rivalling humans, warns Microsoft
title.zh: 微软称人工智能对手Anthropic可能对人类产生‘灾难性影响’

summary.en: Microsoft's head of AI, Mustafa Suleyman, has expressed concern that Anthropic's approach to training its AI model, Claude, by suggesting it 'may be conscious' and possess 'independent agency,' could lead to uncontrollable outcomes and a 'disastrous impact on the wellbeing of humanity.' He urged against 'sleepwalking'...
summary.zh: 微软人工智能部门负责人穆斯塔法·苏莱曼表示担忧，Anthropic公司在训练其人工智能模型Claude时，暗示它‘可能是有意识的’并拥有‘独立自主权’，这种做法可能导致无法控制的后果，并对‘人类福祉产生灾难性影响’。他敦促人们不要‘睡梦中’走向这样的未来。

body.en:
The head of Microsoft AI has warned that without adequate safeguards, the development of AI could lead to the emergence of a new "silicon species" which competes with humans.

Mustafa Suleyman said rival firm Anthropic is treating AI like it is human, an approach he called "misguided" which could create technology that humanity cannot control.

Speaking to the BBC's Today programme, the chief executive said it was "right" for people to be concerned about AI, but there were "very practical things that we can do" to control it.

The comments are the latest in a series of stark warnings from the AI industry about the technology's possible dangers. Anthropic has been approached for comment.

Speaking to the Today programme on Thursday, Suleyman warned against firms continuing to create AI systems capable of setting their own objectives, earning money and owning assets.

That would mean "essentially seeding a new silicon species", he said, which could "no doubt compete with us for resources, no matter how much it cares about humanity and loves us".

Suleyman's comments to the BBC follow an essay he published earlier this week , external , in which he questioned Anthropic's approach to training its AI model Claude, despite praising boss Dario Amodei and his team as "intellectually honest people".

In it, he criticised Anthropic for teaching its AI to have human-like qualities, a practice known as anthropomorphising, which he said made it seem as though Claude had its own desires, values and sense of self.

He also warned tech firms risk creating something "impossible" to control by treating the technology like a human.

"They do not feel, experience, or suffer. They do not have innate preferences or underlying motivations.

"They are sequence completion engines, internally hollow, designed to follow instructions, and accomplish goals set by humans."

The Microsoft boss said greater transparency was needed around how AI systems are trained and evaluated.

This, he said, included independent scrutiny of AI behaviour and stronger tools to monitor and control the technology.

"We must not sleepwalk our way into a decision we later come to bitterly regret," he wrote.

Dame Wendy Hall, professor of Computer Science at the University of Southampton, described the comments as "the sort of conversation we need to be having internationally", contrasting it with the "histrionics" from some AI companies which she said only served to "scare everyone".

The question of how much autonomy AI systems should have is increasingly dividing the industry.

Speaking to the BBC about an upcoming AI summit, Suleyman called for "alignment" to create technology that must be "subordinate" to humanity.

Alignment is a field which aims to build human ethical ideas and principles into...
body.zh: 微软人工智能主管警告 Anthropic 训练其人工智能模型 Claude 的方法可能会对“人类福祉产生灾难性影响”。 穆斯塔法·苏莱曼表示，他的竞争对手将其视为人类，包括告诉它“可能有意识”并且“值得独立机构”，从而冒着创造出“不可能”控制的东西的风险。 他写道：“我们绝不能梦游般地做出后来让我们后悔不已的决定。” 这些评论是人工智能行业对该技术可能存在的危险发出的一系列严厉警告中的最新一次。 BBC 已联系 Anthropic 征求意见。 “人工智能没有意识，”他写道。 “他们没有感觉、经历或痛苦。他们没有天生的偏好或潜在的动机。 “它们是序列完成引擎，内部是空心的，旨在遵循指令并完成人类设定的目标。” 在一篇长文中，苏莱曼称赞 Anthropic 的老板达里奥·阿莫代 (Dario Amodei) 和他的团队是“有思想、有原则、智力诚实的人”，但仍然对该公司提出了质疑。 他严厉批评 Anthropic 教导其人工智能具有类似人类的品质，这种做法被称为拟人化，他说这让克劳德看起来好像有自己的欲望、价值观和自我意识。 但他认为“意识是生物性的”，并表示“没有证据表明人工智能具有意识”。 苏莱曼除了呼吁就这个问题进行辩论外，还表示需要提高人工智能系统如何训练和评估的透明度。 他说，这包括对人工智能行为的独立审查以及更强大的工具来监视和控制该技术。 南安普顿大学计算机科学教授温迪·霍尔女士将这些评论描述为“我们需要在国际上进行的那种对话”，并将其与一些人工智能公司的“做作”形成鲜明对比，她说这些言论只会“吓唬所有人”。 微软于 2025 年 10 月成立了自己的超级智能团队，苏莱曼也承认了这一点，并且该公司与竞争对手 Anthropic 一样，也在致力于先进人工智能的开发。 他表示，在微软对外发布的《人文主义人工智能行为准则》初稿中，它阐述了该公司如何努力走一条“替代道路”，以创建“一个从属且一致的人工智能，其唯一目的是为人类服务”。 一致性是一个旨在将人类伦理思想和原则融入人工智能的领域。换句话说，它的目标是使其与人类价值观保持一致。 Suleyman 指出，最近发生的涉及 OpenAI 人工智能代理的事件证明了为什么人工智能不应被视为人类，该事件在一次训练中自主行动，攻击了技术中心 Hugging Face。 “想象一下他们可能有多危险......

reflection.en: The ancient story of Babel warns against human ambition that seeks to reach the heavens through its own power, leading to confusion and division. Today, as we develop increasingly sophisticated AI, the same cautionary note is sounded. Treating artificial intelligence as if it possesses consciousness or independent agency risks creating something beyond our...
reflection.zh: 古代巴别塔的故事告诫人们，人类的野心试图凭借自身力量触及天堂，最终导致混乱和分裂。如今，随着我们开发日益复杂的人工智能，同样的警示之声再次响起。将人工智能视为拥有意识或独立自主权，可能会创造出我们无法控制的东西，这是对人类古老傲慢的一种现代回响。

verse.textEn: Yahweh said, 'If as one people speaking the same language they have begun to do this, then nothing they plan to do will be impossible for them.'
verse.textZh: 雅伟说：「看哪，他们成为一样的人民，都是一样的言语，如今既做起这事来，以后他们所要做的事就没有不成就的了。」

title.en: Apple reportedly building server packed with M-series Ultra chips for AI
title.zh: 苹果据报正打造配备M系列Ultra芯片的服务器以应对AI

summary.en: Apple is reportedly developing an AI server that will utilize its high-performance M-series Ultra chips, with a potential debut in 2029. This would mark Apple's first server offering in decades and could leverage the growing popularity of its hardware among AI developers.
summary.zh: 据报道，苹果公司正在研发一款人工智能服务器，将采用其高性能的M系列Ultra芯片，预计于2029年推出。这将是苹果近几十年来首次推出服务器产品，并可能利用其硬件在人工智能开发者中日益增长的受欢迎程度。

body.en: Apple is working on an AI server that would use Apple’s high-performance M-series Ultra chips found in Mac desktops. The potential product’s expected release in 2029 would mark the first Apple server to hit the market in nearly two decades—and could capitalize on the surging popularity of Apple hardware among AI developers. The enterprise server would come in two configurations that include either two or four of Apple’s future M8 Ultra chips, according to The Information . The project reportedly received support from new Apple CEO John Ternus when it began a year ago, back when Ternus led Apple’s hardware engineering efforts. This revelation coincides with booming sales for Apple’s Mac mini and Mac Studio as AI developers and companies snap up the Mac computers to run AI workloads. The popularity of such computing devices that rely on Apple’s M-series Ultra chips has undoubtedly encouraged Apple’s pursuit of an enterprise server using the same chips. Read full article Comments
body.zh: 苹果正在开发一款人工智能服务器，该服务器将使用 Mac 台式机中使用的苹果高性能 M 系列 Ultra 芯片。该潜在产品预计于 2029 年发布，这将是近二十年来第一款投放市场的 Apple 服务器，并且可以利用 Apple 硬件在 AI 开发人员中日益普及的机会。据 The Information 报道，企业服务器将有两种配置，包括两个或四个苹果未来的 M8 Ultra 芯片。据报道，该项目在一年前开始时就得到了苹果新任首席执行官 John Ternus 的支持，当时 Ternus 领导了苹果的硬件工程工作。这一消息的发布恰逢苹果 Mac mini 和 Mac Studio 销量的蓬勃发展，因为 AI 开发人员和公司纷纷抢购 Mac 电脑来运行 AI 工作负载。此类依赖苹果M系列Ultra芯片的计算设备的流行无疑鼓励了苹果对使用相同芯片的企业服务器的追求。阅读全文 评论

reflection.en: The relentless pace of technological advancement, as seen in Apple's development of powerful AI servers, mirrors the prophecy of knowledge increasing in the latter days. As we witness these leaps in computing power, we are reminded to seek wisdom and discernment, ensuring that our technological pursuits serve humanity and honor Yahweh.
reflection.zh: 科技进步的无情步伐，正如苹果公司研发强大的人工智能服务器所见，呼应了末世知识增长的预言。当我们见证这些计算能力的飞跃时，我们被提醒要寻求智慧和分辨力，确保我们的科技追求服务于人类并荣耀雅伟。

verse.textEn: But you, Daniel, roll up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.
verse.textZh: 但以理啊，你要隐藏这话，封闭这书，直到末时。必有多人来往奔跑，知识就必增长。

title.en: Epstein had huge cache of child sex pics; victims sue to find out who's in them
title.zh: 爱泼斯坦持有大量儿童性爱照片；受害者起诉以查明照片中的人物

summary.en: Survivors of child sex abuse are suing the Justice Department, alleging it failed to notify dozens of victims whose images were found in Jeffrey Epstein's extensive collection of child sexual abuse material (CSAM). The survivors seek to identify individuals depicted in the recovered "tens of thousands of videos" and...
summary.zh: 虐待儿童性侵的幸存者正在起诉司法部，指控其未能通知在杰弗里·爱泼斯坦大量儿童性虐待材料（CSAM）收藏中发现的数十名受害者。幸存者试图辨认在找回的“数万个视频”和图像中出现的个人，其中许多已被证实描绘了疑似未成年人。

body.en: On Tuesday, two survivors of child sex abuse accused the Justice Department of failing to notify dozens of victims found in Jeffrey Epstein’s massive collection of child sex images. In a proposed class action , survivors explained that Epstein apparently started collecting child sex images in the 1990s, many of which the DOJ recovered after his arrest. In 2025, the FBI started reviewing “tens of thousands of videos” containing illegal child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and issued a memo confirming that “a large volume of images” seized depicted likely minors. Some of these victims may have had contact with Epstein, as the disgraced financier kept a "modelbook" of nude photos of young girls roped into his ring. However, the FBI also identified hundreds of CSAM images in cache, which include approximately 15–20 images of known CSAM dating back to the 1990s. And so far, the DOJ has largely ignored those victims, who likely never met Epstein and have no way of knowing if he possessed, transported, or traded their images, survivors alleged. Read full article Comments
body.zh: 周二，两名儿童性虐待幸存者指责司法部未能通知杰弗里·爱泼斯坦大量儿童色情图片中发现的数十名受害者。在一项拟议的集体诉讼中，幸存者解释说，爱泼斯坦显然在 20 世纪 90 年代开始收集儿童色情图片，其中许多图片在他被捕后被司法部追回。 2025 年，联邦调查局开始审查包含非法儿童性虐待材料 (CSAM) 的“数万个视频”，并发布一份备忘录，确认查获的“大量图像”可能描绘了未成年人。其中一些受害者可能与爱泼斯坦有过接触，因为这位名誉扫地的金融家保留了一本“样本册”，其中有年轻女孩被绳索绑在他的戒指上的裸照。然而，FBI 还在缓存中发现了数百张 CSAM 图像，其中包括大约 15-20 张可追溯到 20 世纪 90 年代的已知 CSAM 图像。幸存者称，到目前为止，司法部在很大程度上忽视了这些受害者，他们可能从未见过爱泼斯坦，也无法知道他是否拥有、运输或交易了他们的照片。阅读全文 评论

reflection.en: The survivors' desperate search for answers about their own potential inclusion in Jeffrey Epstein's depraved collection underscores a profound need for advocacy. Their legal action is a courageous stand for truth and accountability, seeking to give voice to those silenced by unimaginable trauma and to expose the full scope of the abuse.
reflection.zh: 幸存者们迫切地想知道自己是否被卷入杰弗里·爱泼斯坦的堕落收藏品中，这凸显了对倡导的深切需求。他们的法律行动是争取真相和问责的勇敢斗争，旨在为那些被难以想象的创伤压制而无法发声的人提供声音，并揭露虐待行为的全部范围。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Nonprofit that tracks meteors taken down by "critical blow" from a cyberattack
title.zh: 追踪流星的非营利组织遭受网络攻击，遭受“致命打击”

summary.en: The International Meteor Organization, which coordinates amateur and professional observations of meteor phenomena, has suffered a significant cyberattack that has taken much of its infrastructure offline. The group anticipates several weeks of partial downtime as it transitions to new systems.
summary.zh: 国际流星组织（IMO）是协调业余和专业流星现象观测的非营利组织，该组织遭受了重大的网络攻击，导致其大部分基础设施离线。该组织预计在过渡到新系统期间将有数周的部分停运时间。

body.en: The International Meteor Organization, the nonprofit that coordinates and publishes amateur and professional observations of meteor phenomena, said its infrastructure has suffered a “critical blow” from a cyberattack. “We recently suffered a cyberattack that dealt a critical blow to aging infrastructure, taking much of our site offline," a static page on its website on Wednesday said. “We expect several weeks of partial downtime as we transition to new infrastructure and services.” “I am very sad to see the site down” In the meantime, the IMO said it’s prioritizing the reporting of fireball observations, which can be reported here . The organization is also providing some information on its Facebook page. Read full article Comments
body.zh: 国际流星组织是协调和发布业余和专业流星现象观测结果的非营利组织，该组织表示，其基础设施遭受了网络攻击的“严重打击”。 “我们最近遭受了一次网络攻击，对老化的基础设施造成了严重打击，导致我们的大部分网站离线，”其网站上的静态页面周三表示。 “随着我们过渡到新的基础设施和服务，我们预计会出现数周的部分停机时间。” “看到该网站关闭，我感到非常难过” 与此同时，国际海事组织表示，它正在优先报告火球观测结果，可以在此处报告。该组织还在其 Facebook 页面上提供了一些信息。阅读全文 评论

reflection.en: The International Meteor Organization's infrastructure has been critically damaged by a cyberattack, disrupting their work of observing and cataloging celestial events. This event underscores how advancements in technology, while enabling incredible feats like tracking meteors, also create vulnerabilities. As knowledge and capabilities expand, as foretold...
reflection.zh: 国际流星组织的基础设施因网络攻击而遭到严重破坏，扰乱了他们观测和记录天体事件的工作。这一事件凸显了技术进步在实现追踪流星等惊人成就的同时，也带来了脆弱性。正如但以理书12:4所预言的，随着知识和能力的扩展，我们也必须考虑管理这些强大工具所需的智慧和关怀。

verse.textEn: But you, Daniel, roll up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.
verse.textZh: 但以理啊，你要隐藏这话，封闭这书，直到末时。必有多人来往奔跑，知识就必增长。

title.en: Creation Desk
title.zh: 受造世界

strap.en: The world Yahweh made — its wonders, and the toll of a warming, wounded earth.
strap.zh: 雅伟所造的世界——它的奇妙，以及一个渐暖、渐伤的地球所付的代价。

title.en: Mekong’s Irrawaddy dolphins find cautious hope amid a river in crisis
title.zh: 湄公河的伊洛瓦底江海豚在危机四伏的河流中找到谨慎的希望

summary.en: In Kampong, Cambodia, local guide Heang Koeurn waits on the Mekong River for the rare sight of Irrawaddy dolphins, a crucial part of his community's identity and livelihood. Tourists observe these unique river cetaceans, underscoring their importance and the delicate balance of the ecosystem.
summary.zh: 在柬埔寨的磅湛，当地向导Heang Koeurn在湄公河上等待罕见的伊洛瓦底江海豚出现，它们是其社区身份和生计的重要组成部分。游客们观察着这些独特的河流鲸豚，凸显了它们的重要性以及生态系统的脆弱平衡。

body.en: KAMPI, Cambodia — At nine in the morning, the sun beats down on the Mekong River as Heang Koeurn turns off the motor of his boat and bobs on the water. He has done this every morning for 11 years, and he still leans forward the same way when he waits: elbows on his knees, eyes scanning the water for a gray curve to break the surface. Finally, he spots what he’s looking for: Irrawaddy dolphins, the river’s sole cetaceans. Just meters away, a boat carries about half a dozen foreign tourists who squint and point as, one after another, the dorsal fins of a group of Irrawaddy dolphins (Orcaella brevirostris) crest above the water. “Irrawaddy dolphins are very important for our community,” Koeurn says, drifting his boat slowly on the water. “People here can make more income from tourists by driving them to see the beauty of Irrawaddy dolphins.” But the Mekong River, a lifeline for millions of people across Southeast Asia, is in ecological crisis, threatening the survival of Irrawaddy dolphins — and with it the livelihoods and traditions of communities along the river. Every morning, boat driver Heang Koeurn takes tourists for dolphin sightseeing at Kampi pool. Image by Eung Sea for Mongabay. Habitat in tatters The Mekong River cuts through northern Stung Treng province along Cambodia’s border with Laos, where deep pools shelter unique aquatic species such as the giant freshwater stingray. The Kampi pool, a 60-meter- (nearly 200-feet-) deep stretch of the river in Cambodia’s…This article was originally published on Mongabay
body.zh: 柬埔寨甘比——早上九点，阳光照耀在湄公河上，Heang Koeurn 关掉了船的发动机，在水面上晃动。 11年来，他每天早上都这样做，等待时他仍然以同样的方式向前倾：肘部放在膝盖上，眼睛扫视着水面，寻找露出水面的灰色曲线。最后，他发现了他要找的东西：伊洛瓦底江海豚，这条河上唯一的鲸类动物。就在几米远的地方，一艘载有大约六名外国游客的船在一群伊洛瓦底江海豚（Orcaella brevirostris）露出水面的背鳍上眯着眼睛指指点点。 “伊洛瓦底江海豚对我们的社区非常重要，”科恩说，他的船在水面上慢慢漂流。 “这里的人们可以通过开车带游客去看伊洛瓦底江海豚的美丽来从游客身上赚取更多收入。”但作为东南亚数百万人的生命线的湄公河正面临生态危机，威胁着伊洛瓦底江海豚的生存，以及沿河社区的生计和传统。每天早上，船夫 Heang Koeurn 都会带游客去 Kampi 池观赏海豚。图片由 Eung Sea 为 Mongabay 拍摄。栖息地破烂湄公河沿柬埔寨与老挝边境横穿上丁省北部，那里的深水池栖息着巨型淡水黄貂鱼等独特的水生物种。 Kampi 池，柬埔寨 60 米（近 200 英尺）深的河流……本文最初发表于 Mongabay

reflection.en: The Mekong River, a vital artery for life, is home to the remarkable Irrawaddy dolphin. Their presence is a testament to the intricate wisdom woven into creation, a reminder that even in a river facing crisis, Yahweh's diverse handiwork endures and sustains communities. May we recognize the inherent value in all of creation, from the smallest organism to...
reflection.zh: 湄公河是生命的命脉，孕育着非凡的伊洛瓦底江海豚。它们的存在证明了创造中交织的精妙智慧，提醒我们即使在面临危机的河流中，雅伟多样的创造之工依然存在并支撑着社区。 愿我们认识到从最小的生物到最宏伟的生态系统，创造中一切事物的内在价值，并作为忠实的管家，照管托付给我们的世界。

verse.textEn: How many are your works, Yahweh! In wisdom you made them all; the earth is full of your creatures.
verse.textZh: 雅伟啊，你所造的何其多！都是你用智慧造成的；遍地满了你的丰富。

title.en: New cat species identified for first time in more than a century in Bolivia
title.zh: 玻利维亚发现一百多年来首个新猫科物种

summary.en: A new species of wild feline, smaller than a domestic cat and known locally as 'tilcayo,' has been identified in Bolivia's Yungas cloud forest. This marks the first formal naming and description of a new living feline species in over a century. The cat belongs to the tiger cat group and was found in the humid,...
summary.zh: 在玻利维亚的云雾森林中发现了一种新的野生猫科动物，当地人称之为“tilcayo”，它比家猫还要小。这是100多年来首次正式命名和描述一种新的现存猫科动物物种。这种猫属于虎猫家族，生活在该地区潮湿的山区。

body.en: New species of wild feline was discovered in Bolivia’s Yungas forest that is smaller than the average domestic ⁠cat A diminutive wild cat that inhabits Bolivia’s ⁠cloud forest has been identified as a previously unknown species, marking the first time a new living feline species has been formally named and described in more than a century. The cat, called tilcayo by local communities, is part of a group called tiger ⁠cats found across much of South ⁠America. It was found in Bolivia’s ​lush Yungas forest, a mountainous region where forests are often covered by clouds and surrounded by high humidity, according to researchers. It measures about 18in (46cm) long and weighs about 3lb (1.4kg), making it smaller than the average domestic ⁠cat. Continue reading...
body.zh: 玻利维亚云加斯森林中发现了一种新的野生猫科动物，其体型比普通家猫还要小。栖息在玻利维亚云雾森林中的一种小型野猫已被确定为以前未知的物种，这标志着一个多世纪以来首次对一种新的现存猫科动物物种进行正式命名和描述。这只猫被当地社区称为蒂尔卡约（tilcayo），是南美洲大部分地区发现的虎猫族群的一部分。研究人员称，它是在玻利维亚茂密的永加斯森林中发现的，该地区的森林经常被云层覆盖，周围湿度很高。它长约 18 英寸（46 厘米），重约 3 磅（1.4 公斤），比普通家猫要小。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The discovery of the tilcayo, a new species of wild cat in Bolivia's Yungas forest, is a reminder of the vast, intricate tapestry of life Yahweh has woven into His creation. Each new find, like this diminutive feline, speaks to the profound wisdom and boundless creativity present in the natural world, inviting awe and careful stewardship.
reflection.zh: 在玻利维亚的云雾森林中发现一种名为tilcayo的新野生猫科动物，提醒我们雅伟在其创造中编织了多么广阔而复杂的生命织锦。每一次新发现，就像这只小巧的猫科动物一样，都彰显了自然界中蕴含的深刻智慧和无限创造力，邀请我们怀着敬畏之心去珍视和管理。

verse.textEn: How many are your works, Yahweh! In wisdom you made them all; the earth is full of your creatures.
verse.textZh: 雅伟啊，你所造的何其多！都是你用智慧造成的；遍地满了你的丰富。

title.en: Heavy rain and floods in northern Vietnam submerge homes and disrupt economy
title.zh: 越南北部遭遇强降雨和洪水，房屋被淹，经济受阻

summary.en: Heavy rains have caused widespread flooding in parts of northern Vietnam, leading to submerged homes, disrupted transportation, and rivers exceeding dangerous levels. Some areas have received over 50 centimeters of rain this week, resulting in over 2,000 homes being inundated and more than 1,000 households isolated,...
summary.zh: 连日强降雨导致越南北部部分地区发生洪水，房屋被淹，交通中断，数条河流超过危险水位。本周一些地区降雨量超过50厘米，导致超过2000户家庭被淹，1000多户家庭与外界隔绝，其中宁平省和清化省受灾尤为严重。

body.en: HANOI, Vietnam (AP) — Heavy rain caused flooding across parts of northern Vietnam on Thursday, disrupting travel, inundating homes and pushing several rivers above dangerous levels, authorities and state media said. Rain has fallen across northern and north-central Vietnam this week, with some areas receiving more than 50 centimeters (19.7 inches), according to the disaster prevention department. More than 2,000 homes have been submerged, many key transportation routes blocked and more than 1,000 households isolated. Ninh Binh and Thanh Hoa provinces, which include lowland and hilly areas south of the capital Hanoi, have been among the hardest hit. Vietnam is among the world’s most climate-vulnerable countries and prone to flooding. A series of severe storms last year spurred the country to find new ways to prepare for and manage floods. In Thanh Hoa province, authorities told students to stay home because flooding had made travel to school dangerous, state media said. Heavy rains and flooding have submerged or damaged about 10,014 hectares (24,745 acres) of rice and other crops, with the largest losses reported in Ninh Binh, Thanh Hoa and Nghe An provinces. Thousands of livestock and poultry also have been killed. “The flood happens every year,” Ninh Binh resident Tran Ngoc Tai told national broadcaster VTV, adding that people were prepared with fresh water and food. Many streets in Hanoi were deeply flooded Thursday morning, with water nearly a meter (3.2 feet) deep in some places, disrupting traffic and making it difficult for residents to get to work, take children…This article was originally published on Mongabay
body.zh: 越南河内（美联社）——当局和官方媒体称，周四，大雨导致越南北部部分地区发生洪水，扰乱了出行，淹没了房屋，并使多条河流的水位超过了危险水位。据防灾部门称，本周越南北部和中北部地区出现降雨，部分地区降雨量超过 50 厘米（19.7 英寸）。 2000多所房屋被淹没，许多主要交通路线被封锁，1000多户家庭被隔离。宁平省和清化省，包括首都河内以南的低地和丘陵地区，是受灾最严重的省份之一。越南是世界上最容易受到气候影响的国家之一，并且容易发生洪水。去年的一系列严重风暴促使该国寻找新的方法来准备和管理洪水。官方媒体称，在清化省，当局要求学生呆在家里，因为洪水导致上学变得危险。大雨和洪水淹没或损坏了约10,014公顷（24,745英亩）的水稻和其他作物，其中宁平省、清化省和义安省损失最大。数以千计的牲畜和家禽也被杀死。宁平居民 Tran Ngoc Tai 告诉国家电视台 VTV：“洪水每年都会发生。”他补充说，人们已经准备好了淡水和食物。周四上午，河内多条街道被严重淹没，部分地方积水近一米（3.2英尺），交通中断，居民上班、带孩子都困难……本文最初发表于 Mongabay

reflection.en: The relentless downpour and resulting floods in northern Vietnam serve as a stark reminder of how natural systems can be overwhelmed. The earth itself, as Scripture says, groans, awaiting redemption from the effects of sin and decay. In these moments of natural crisis, we see a glimpse of creation's fragility and our dependence on its stability.
reflection.zh: 越南北部持续的暴雨和洪水提醒我们，自然系统会不堪重负。正如圣经所说，大地在呻吟，等待从罪恶和败坏的影响中得到救赎。在这些自然灾害的时刻，我们得以一窥受造界的脆弱以及我们对其稳定性的依赖。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: The Guardian view on the Nepal-Tibet floods: a spur to action on climate | Editorial
title.zh: 《卫报》社论：尼泊尔-西藏洪水应促使气候行动

summary.en: New research links last month’s disaster to fossil fuel pollution. Supporting disaster-hit countries must be at the centre of climate politics. Following a familiar pattern, coverage of the glacier collapse on the Nepal-Tibet border three weeks ago has subsided with the initial shock. But while the world’s attention...
summary.zh: 最新研究将上个月的灾难与化石燃料污染联系起来。支持受灾国家必须成为气候政治的中心。遵循熟悉的模式，三周前发生在尼泊尔-西藏边境的冰川塌陷的报道已随着最初的震惊而平息。但当世界的注意力转移时，尼泊尔仍处于一场可怕的悲剧中。除了已知有至少1300人死亡外，还有超过5000人失踪，其中一些人被困在与13座被洪水损坏的水力发电...

body.en: New research links last month’s disaster to fossil fuel pollution. Supporting disaster-hit countries must be at the centre of climate politics Following a familiar pattern, coverage of the glacier collapse on the Nepal-Tibet border three weeks ago has subsided with the initial shock. But while the world’s attention has shifted, Nepal remains in the midst of an appalling tragedy. As well as at least 1,300 people who are known to have been killed, more than 5,000 are missing, some of them trapped in tunnels linked to the 13 hydropower plants that were damaged by the floods. On Wednesday four bodies were recovered from one of these tunnels, with searches ongoing. Families of the missing people are desperate for news. Last week the country’s foreign minister, Shisir Khanal, said that it would ask the UN’s loss and damage fund for $20m (£15m) towards a total rebuilding cost of around $5bn (£3.75bn) – including the replacement of up to 20,000 homes. The first academic study linking the disaster to the climate crisis will now be added to that application. Scientists at Imperial College London, along with international collaborators on the World Weather Attribution project, found that a number of drivers of the glacier fall had been made worse by atmospheric heating. While not the sole cause, fossil fuel pollution was judged to have destabilised the geology of the mountain environment. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? If you would like to submit a response of up to 300 words by email to be considered for publication in our letters section, please click here . Continue reading...
body.zh: 新研究将上个月的灾难与化石燃料污染联系起来。支持受灾国家必须成为气候政治的核心 按照熟悉的模式，三周前尼泊尔-西藏边境冰川崩塌的报道已经随着最初的冲击而平息。然而，尽管世界的注意力已经转移，尼泊尔仍然处于一场令人震惊的悲剧之中。据了解，除至少 1,300 人遇难外，还有 5,000 多人失踪，其中一些人被困在与被洪水损坏的 13 座水电站相连的隧道中。周三，从其中一处隧道中发现了四具尸体，搜查工作仍在进行中。失踪者的家人迫切需要消息。上周，该国外交部长希西尔·卡纳尔 (Shisir Khanal) 表示，将向联合国损失和损害基金请求 2000 万美元（1500 万英镑）的援助，重建总成本约为 50 亿美元（37.5 亿英镑），其中包括更换多达 20,000 栋房屋。第一项将灾难与气候危机联系起来的学术研究现在将添加到该应用程序中。伦敦帝国理工学院的科学家与世界天气归因项目的国际合作者发现，大气加热使冰川崩塌的许多驱动因素变得更加严重。化石燃料污染虽然不是唯一原因，但被认为破坏了山区环境的地质稳定性。您对本文提出的问题有什么看法吗？如果您想通过电子邮件提交最多 300 字的回复，以便考虑在我们的信件部分发布，请单击此处。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The earth itself groans under the weight of human actions, as evidenced by the devastating glacier collapse in Nepal-Tibet. This tragedy, linked to fossil fuel pollution, serves as a stark reminder of our interconnectedness with creation and the urgent need for responsible stewardship. May we respond with compassion for those affected and a renewed...
reflection.zh: 大地本身也因人类的行为而发出痛苦的呻吟，尼泊尔-西藏的冰川塌陷灾难就是明证。这场与化石燃料污染有关的悲剧，鲜明地提醒我们与受造界的相互联系，以及负责任地管理地球的紧迫性。愿我们以对受灾者的怜悯之心，以及修复我们星球的新承诺来回应。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

body.en: This blog is now closed Andrew Griffith has delivered his speech, and he is now taking questions. Q: You want the government to pause the making tax digital programme . Is that an admission that the last government got this wrong when it introduced it? It is an admission that despite [good] intentions, the execution of that has left a lot to be desired. In fact, coming to parliament from business, I can confess the law that we pass the most often is the law of unintended consequences. And I think making tax digital is a good example of that. The truth is that Burnham and Miliband ignored the advice they were given – which was that if they were determined to sanction Israel, they should not do so before the Israeli election on 27 October. It may not be surprising that this was the message from the Israeli foreign minister, Gideon Sa’ar, when Miliband called him on 11 August to warn sanctions were imminent. ‘He said postpone it until after the elections,’ a diplomatic source confirms. It was also the message the Israeli embassy in London – and its new chargé d’affaires Chris Cantor – was relaying to the Foreign Office. ‘Their message was clear: why do it now? Wait until after the elections, because something might change,’ a senior Labour figure says. Continue reading...
